docs.title: oCen_stream: the Omega Centauri stream and the Milky Way bar
docs.text:
Goal. Constrain the Milky Way bar (pattern speed Ωb, angle, amplitude, size), the halo flattening q, the circular speed vc and the cluster's distance and proper motion by fitting particle-spray models of the Omega Centauri tidal stream (STREAMFINDER stream 54, Fimbulthul; Ibata et al. 2024) in Gaia DR3.

This work started inside oCen_dm and moved here on 2026-10-25 with its history. The pages under History and Reviews describe the state before that date.

docs.title: Status (2026-10-25)
docs.text:
• Data vector (25 numbers). Sky: one-Gaussian fits in seven 3° windows along φ1 (track and width; no branch cut; φ1 6–9° dropped). Proper motions: spline tracks of μα* and μδ at their knots (6 and 5), with full covariance. Errors are used as measured.
  • Score. Each model is measured exactly like the data (same masks, same fits); χ² of data minus model with data and model (bootstrap) errors; no nuisance terms.
  • Rescoring of 2,369 stored models. The best scores χ² = 166; the best model without a bar scores 598.
  • Free 9-parameter fit (Nelder–Mead, 4 chains, 40 steps each). Best: χ² = 165.5 ± 1.4 (four 256k-particle seeds) at angle 14°, Ωb 33 km/s/kpc, amplitude 1.27, size 1.44, q 0.80, vc 222 km/s, distance 5.67 kpc. The search did not improve on its starting point. The three good chains agree on Ωb ≈ 32–34 and angle ≈ 14–18°; q, distance and size are not pinned down; vc and distance sit at their range limits. The chains stayed near their starts, so this is not a posterior.
  • Remaining misfits. The model stream is too wide at φ1 0–3° and 21–24°; μα* and μδ miss at the end knots.

docs.title: How to navigate
docs.text:
• Data: the stream sample, Gaia errors, derived geometry and caches; potentials and frames.
  • Status up to 2026-10-18, likelihood versions, results index.
  • Reviews and literature.

docs.title: Stream 54 fit: diagnostic and model-extension plan (2026-10-10; Phase 3 adopted the same day)
docs.text:
Historical (2026-10-10)

Superseded; current status: kb/stream_status.md. Stale claims below:

  • "Omega_b = 34-35 robust to every variation" holds only at fixed bar size.
  • Phases marked "running now" are done.
  • The spray-noise numbers are superseded: the legacy score does not converge with particle number (kb/models/stream_likelihood_versions.md).
  • The LMC (M6, item 6) was done on 2026-10-12/13.
  • "No grid below 16 deg" is superseded by the 9-D emulator design (bar angle 10-35 deg).

Built from: STREAM_FIT_CAMPAIGN_PLAN.md, STREAM_FIT_METHODS_REVIEW.md, Codex reviews codex_likelihood_calibration_2026-10-09.md, codex_diagnostic_experiments_2026-10-10.md, codex_code_review_2026-10-10.md, and the journal (2026-10-09/10).

docs.title: Where we are
docs.text:
• A rotating bar is the only ingredient found so far that makes the knee. Omega_b = 34-35 km/s/kpc is robust to every variation tried.
  • Two problems remain:
  • P1. The knee is not fully reproduced. Beyond phi1 ~ 20 deg, model pmdec stays 0.5-1 mas/yr too high, and the model debris thins out.
  • P2. The fit wants an implausible bar. It prefers angle 16 deg (literature ~27) with amplitude 1.4. The 20-deg model fits better near the cluster, the 16-deg model better in the knee.
  • Ruled out:
  • code errors: bar clock, r_J derivatives, centre orbit, frame round trip, arm/chi labels, data integrity, bar near end and rotation sense;
  • cluster internal rotation, even x10;
  • the debris age cut (500-1000 Myr);
  • kernel width;
  • Sgr;
  • axisymmetric hosts.
  • Statistics: lnL is overconfident. Spray noise is +-120 at 1x and +-36 at 4x particles, and misfit is correlated over many degrees. Calibration has to come from mocks.

docs.title: Phase 1 -- diagnostics (running now; ~1 h of CPU in total)
docs.text:
Question Design Decision rule Cost D1 What drives the angle preference: which stretch of the stream, which observable? Best model at each angle (16, 20, 24, 28), 4x particles, seed 1. Per-star lnL split into phi1 segments (< 4, 4-17, > 17) and into per-observable conditional scores (dphi2; PM pair; v_los). If the preference comes from one segment AND one observable, that localises the missing physics. If it is spread out, suspect the statistic. 1 spray (24 deg at 4x) + minutes of scoring D2 Does the method itself pull towards low angles? Mock members drawn from truth sprays at 28 and 20 deg (seed 7, 4x; independent of the candidate sprays). Same phi1 values, Gaia covariances and v_los pattern as the data. 100 mocks per truth, scored against 56 candidates (d = 5.6, amp 1.2/1.4, all Omega_b and angles; 1x, seed 1). If 28-deg truths recover 16 deg often, the ranking is untrustworthy. If recovery is good, P2 is physical (model misfit). 2 sprays + ~10 min with 8 processes (timing run first) D3 Is the fixed omega Cen orbit forcing the low angle? At 28 deg (Omega_b 35.5, amp 1.2, d 5.6), a 5x5 grid of pmra, pmdec at catalogue +- 1, 2 sigma (sigma = 0.027 mas/yr), 4x particles, seed 1. A PM shift within 2 sigma that improves the near-cluster and knee segments together, and closes much of the gap to 16 deg, means the state was the problem. 25 sprays x 45 s ~ 19 min (8 threads)

Context for D3: the earlier free-PM optimiser (old chi-KDE likelihood) already moved pmra by about -1 sigma and still drove the angle to the prior edge. A large effect is therefore not expected, but this is the first test with the conditional likelihood.

Gate: - If D2 shows a biased method, fix the statistic before any physics. - If D3 closes the gap, refit with the PMs free. - Otherwise go to Phase 2.

docs.title: Phase 2 -- what the model may be missing (one ingredient at a time, at the literature angle 28 deg)
docs.text:
Each test uses the D1 segment/observable diagnostics against the 28-deg baseline. Success means improving the knee pmdec without losing the near-cluster fit.

Candidate Why plausible Test Cost / status M1 Release prescription (Fardal spray) Codex rated this high. But the 20-deg tracer run misses the knee the same way the spray does. 200k-tracer run vs spray at 28 deg: same host and state; compare footprint medians and counts. ~12 min (8 threads) M2 Slowing bar A decelerating bar was faster in the past; over the ~700 Myr of observed debris the resonances sweep through the orbit, changing the knee and the near-cluster debris differently. Dillamore+2024 prescription (eta = -dOmega/dt / Omega^2), present Omega_b and angle fixed; bar size scales with 1/Omega (existing make_slowing_bar_potential, ../oCen_bar/scripts/ocen_bar_common.py; ../chevron_bar_subhalo/src/barchevrons/bar.py). Scan eta = 0 + 3 values. wiring ~1 h; ~1 min per eta at 1x, 4 min at 4x M3 Bar model / length / mass Hunter+2024 is one model. A longer or more massive bar acts like a "strong bar at small angle". (a) Portail+2017 bar (Sormani+2022 approximation; ../oCen_bar/agama_potentials/Portail17.ini) at 28 deg; (b) bar size scaling S (as in make_potential) at fixed angle. wiring ~1 h; minutes of sprays M4 Release history Release is uniform in time, while escape is pericentre-driven. Older debris (> 1 Gyr) may populate the knee. Release window 1500 Myr; pericentre-weighted release (Erkal+2019 style). Compare knee counts and pmdec. minutes M5 Selection (STREAMFINDER) Template-orbit selection could shape the knee PMs. This was planned as Stage 0(b) and never done. Independent Gaia DR3 selection in the knee window (WSDB: sky + CMD + broad PM window, no orbit templates); compare PM ridges with the members. ~1 h of work, seconds of queries M6 Halo shape / LMC Affects the orbit over Gyr. Less likely to produce a sharp knee. Only if M1-M5 fail: one flattened halo and one LMC+reflex variant (no LMC in the code yet). days (LMC)

Literature for M2/M3: Dillamore, Belokurov & Evans 2024, MNRAS 532, 4389 (arXiv:2402.14907); Sormani+2022, MNRAS 514, L1 (ADS, arXiv:2204.13114); Portail+2017, MNRAS 465, 1621 (ADS, arXiv:1608.07954). Present-day bar deceleration rates from the literature are to be looked up before choosing eta (UNVERIFIED).

docs.title: Status after Phases 1-2 (2026-10-10; numbers in the project journal, local)
docs.text:
• Not the cause:
  • code: audits and end-to-end checks pass;
  • method: D2 mocks recover the true angle (28 -> 28 in 100/100; 20 -> 20/24);
  • STREAMFINDER selection: M5 recovers the knee PMs independently to phi1 ~ 24;
  • these ingredients: cluster rotation (even x10), spray release (M1 tracer run is further from the knee), Portail bar, older debris, slowing bar at today's Omega_b.
  • The misfit is two separate problems in the knee:
  • pmra at phi1 15-21: the 28-deg model is ~1 mas/yr too negative. This is all that the low angle fixes; it is the whole angle preference.
  • pmdec at phi1 > 19: every model, at any angle, is ~1 mas/yr too shallow in pmdec. (An earlier claim that the models also put the knee too close rested on our CMD distance track; it is WITHDRAWN: the literature puts the knee at ~0.70-0.75 of omega Cen's distance, and the track's normalisation is flawed -- see codex_distances_and_misfit_2026-10-10.md.)
  • Partial fixes at 28 deg: longer bar (x1.15-1.3: +622/+698); more negative omega Cen PMs (-2 sigma: +518, optimum beyond 2 sigma).

docs.title: Phase 3 -- next (adopted 2026-10-10)
docs.text:
Strategy: avoid unrealistic bar angles. - S1. Give the model the freedom it lacks. The angle is currently the only knob that bends the knee, so the fit uses it. Test whether a longer bar + omega Cen PMs + re-scanned Omega_b reach the 16-deg fit level at 28 deg (Phase 2b grid, running). - S2. DROPPED (2026-10-10). The fit stays distance-free (user decision; CMD track not a calibration, member parallaxes biased high). Original text kept for the record. Add the distance track to the likelihood. At present models are not penalised for putting the knee too close, and 16 deg is barely better there. Including the CMD distance track constrains the model where the angle does not help. Design (to agree): - (a) binned term: model median d/d_ocen of footprint debris per CMD b-bin vs the CMD ratio, with the CMD error plus the model error of the mean; or - (b) per-star photometric distances. Note: next to 3681 per-star terms, a 6-bin term is inert unless the likelihood is calibrated (S3). - S3. Make the angle prior count. With the overconfident likelihood the N(27, 2) prior has no effect. Defensible options: - (a) fix the angle at the literature value and report the remaining misfit as model systematics; - (b) temper the likelihood with an effective sample size calibrated on mocks (D2 machinery). Needs the user's approval.

Physics: improve the stream fit (priority order). 1. Potential shape and mass where the knee lies (was M6; moved up). A 3D mismatch -- too close and too slow in the same region -- points at the force field there, not at the bar's present orientation. - Variants: disc-to-halo mass ratio at fixed v_c(R0), and halo flattening q. - Build them with ../oCen_bar/agama_potentials/example_mw_potential_hunter24.py; its densities are exposed, and the halo is bunched with the central components in one Multipole, so variants need re-construction. - Cost: ~1 h of wiring, then minutes of sprays per variant. Diagnostics: D1 segments, knee PM medians, distance track. 2. Combine the partial fixes (longer bar, omega Cen PMs, Omega_b; slowing bar with Omega_b re-scanned) and measure how much of the gap to 16 deg remains. This is the Phase 2b grid; the pericentre-concentrated release (M4b) is queued after it. 3. ~~Add the distance track to the likelihood (S2)~~ -- dropped. 4. Solar frame x omega Cen distance (Codex, 2026-10-10; next). baumgardt (R0 8.178, V_sun,y 252.24) vs ibata19 (R0 8.122, V_sun,y 232.24) x d_ocen 5.43/5.6/5.8 at the working model (28 deg, bar x1.15, Omega_b 36, amp 1.2) and the 16-deg model; 4x particles; compare knee PM medians and D1 segment lnL. ~12 sprays, ~10 min at 8 threads. 5. Coupled bar angle x longer bar grid (Codex): does the 16-deg preference survive once the longer bar is free? 6. LMC + reflex; alternative progenitor profiles -- expensive, only if 4-5 fail.

docs.title: Phase 4 -- calibration and statistic (after Phase 3)
docs.text:
• Calibrate parameter errors and model comparisons with mocks (D2 machinery). Use seed-averaged densities; use 4x particles in all grids.
  • DM test (on hold by user decision): choose between track-only (conditional) and track+density along the stream (needs a selection model).

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Announce CPU before each launch; one ingredient at a time; no ad hoc error inflation; the bar angle stays near the literature (no grid below 16 deg); journal and commit after each result.

docs.title: Restricted N-body tails with and without DM vs Fimbulthul — scoping (2026-10-08)
docs.text:
Historical (2026-10-08)

Scoping of the restricted N-body experiments. Current status: kb/stream_status.md.

Status: implemented and run (2026-10-08); results and open questions in STREAM_KNEE_INVESTIGATION.md. Decisions marked D1–D5 are the user's.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: How do no DM and different amounts of DM around omega Cen change the structure of its tidal tails? Compare the results with Fimbulthul (Ibata+2019). Tails are made by constrained (restricted) N-body: prescribed host and satellite potentials, with stars as massless tracers (mLCS, Gibbons+2014; streams of Erkal+2019 and Vasiliev+2021).

docs.title: Findings from scoping
docs.text:
1. Within the kinematically allowed models the DM barely changes the escape scale. bin/streams/scope_jacobi.py (results/plot_data/streams_scope_jacobi.json) gives the instantaneous r_J in spherically averaged McMillan17:
model rho20 M_halo (taper 1000 pc) M(<r_J) peri r_J peri / apo [pc] A no DM 0 0 3.24e6 78.7 / 195 rho20scan 0.25 1.7e5 3.28e6 79.0 / 197 0.5 3.5e5 3.32e6 79.3 / 198 1 6.9e5 3.39e6 79.9 / 201 2 1.39e6 3.56e6 81.2 / 207 4 2.78e6 3.91e6 83.8 / 219 B (M/N19 = 9) 2.6 1.81e6 3.63e6 81.8 / 210

The halo is compact (r_s at 5 pc). Its mass inside r_J is offset by a lower M_star, so M(<r_J) rises by at most 21% and r_J by at most 6.5% at pericentre. Stream width and dispersion scale as M^{1/3}, so the expected differences are <~7%. This matches the live runs, where the tail kinematics agree to within 10%. The tails respond to DM beyond ~80–200 pc, which the kinematics do not constrain. The DM axis therefore has to be defined explicitly (D1). 2. Orbit, host potential and integration time dominate. The live 1.96 Gyr McMillan17 debris in the Fimbulthul box has mu_dec = -6 to -9 mas/yr, against -9.7 to -11.5 observed. Ibata+2019 used a static Dehnen & Binney (1998) Model 1, needed >= ~5 Gyr with a rotating progenitor, and found that a non-rotating King progenitor gives a substantially wider stream. Progenitor rotation is therefore a non-DM systematic at least as large as the expected DM signal. 3. The tooling exists in AGAMA 1.0.152; it is not yet in the repo. agama/py/tutorial_streams.ipynb and example_tidal_stream.py provide particle spray (Fardal+2015 as in Gala, and Chen et al. 2025, arXiv:2408.01496), streaklines with linear perturbation, and restricted N-body (Vasiliev+2021). In the restricted scheme, tracers move in host plus moving satellite potential, and the satellite potential and mass are refitted from the bound tracers at intervals, with Chandrasekhar friction optional. Potentials accept time-dependent center= and scale=. 4. Data. Local: I19 Table 1 (309 DR2 candidates, data/processed/tails/fimbulthul_members.ecsv) and 5 CFHT RVs (mean 199.7, rms 5.4 km/s). Also available: the Ibata+2024 DR3 STREAMFINDER atlas (Fimbulthul and the separate Fimbulthul-S), Simpson+2020 (2 GALAH stars) and Kuzma+2026. No intrinsic width, RV dispersion or density has been published. Width and track have to be measured from the candidates. Absolute density is excluded without a STREAMFINDER selection model.

docs.title: Proposed experiment set
docs.text:
• S0 — track (no DM). Use fast spray/mLCS with satellite gravity to find a host, integration time and present-day 6D point that reproduce the Fimbulthul sky, PM, distance and RV track. Candidate hosts: McMillan17 and I19's DB98 Model 1 (D3). Then freeze them. The DM grid must not retune the orbit.
  • S1 — validation. Run restricted N-body for A and B over 1.956 Gyr in static McMillan17, from the same DF samples as the live runs. Compare with the live runs: unbound fraction history, dE/dLz spreads, tail width, near-tail sigma_los and sky track. Tolerances are agreed in advance and tested, not assumed.
  • S2 — DM grid on the frozen S0 orbit: no DM, plus the axis chosen in D1, with tracers of all species. Satellite potential per D2.
  • S3 — comparison in Fimbulthul stream coordinates: phi2(phi1), PM tracks, distance, RV track, width, and (from model tracers only) along-stream density and epicyclic spacing. Apply an approximate STREAMFINDER-like selection (G limit, PM window) to the models.

Cost (estimate, to be benchmarked): spray tracks take seconds to minutes each. Restricted runs with 1e5–1e6 tracers over 2–5 Gyr take of order 10–60 min each with AGAMA's multithreaded integrator, against ~30 h for each live run. No run is launched without a go.

docs.title: Decisions for the user
docs.text:
• D1 DM axis. (a) The rho20 grid at the fitted taper. This is kinematically consistent and the expected result is null at <~7%. (b) Extended halos (taper / M_halo 1e6–1e8) that keep the fitted inner profile, the regime of Vitral & Boldrini 2022, Errani+2022 and Moore 1996. (c) Both: (a) as the control and (b) as the test.
  • D2 Satellite potential. (i) Self-consistent restricted N-body (Vasiliev+2021): halo stripping follows from the tracers, so no hand-tuned halo-loss law is needed. (ii) Strictly prescribed potential (scale= in t, or r_J-truncated halo): closer to "parameterised", but the halo-loss law has to be assumed. Codex: calibrating it on live run B only is circular for the other halos.
  • D3 Host and time. McMillan17 vs DB98 Model 1, 2 Gyr vs ~5 Gyr. A 5 Gyr run needs a progenitor heavier than today's model, and that mass has to be chosen.
  • D4 Rotation. Keep non-rotating now, or add a rotating DF before S2 (I19: rotation matters for width).
  • D5 Data. Done: Ibata+2024 DR3 (streams 54, 55) and Ibata+2021 EDR3 (stream 16) in $OCEN_CATALOGUES/, see configs/data.yaml.

docs.text: Gibbons, Belokurov & Evans 2014, arXiv:1406.2243; Fardal, Huang & Weinberg 2015, arXiv:1410.1861; Küpper, Lane & Heggie 2012, arXiv:1111.5013; Erkal+2019, arXiv:1812.08192; Vasiliev, Belokurov & Erkal 2021, arXiv:2009.10726; Ibata+2019, arXiv:1902.09544 (VizieR J/other/NatAs/3.667); Ibata+2021, arXiv:2012.05245; Ibata+2024, arXiv:2311.17202; Malhan, Valluri & Freese 2021, arXiv:2005.12919; Vitral & Boldrini 2022, arXiv:2112.01265; Errani+2022, arXiv:2203.02513; Evans, Strigari & Zivick 2022, arXiv:2109.10998; Kuzma+2026, arXiv:2605.23474. Codex research pass (ordinary web-research fallback, not Deep Research) supplied the bibliography. The I19 method details (DB98 Model 1, >= 5 Gyr, 1e5 particles, rotating progenitor) are as reported by Codex from the Methods section and are consistent with the journal entry of 2026-09-26. Ibata+2024 (2024ApJ...967...89I) Table 1, fetched 2026-10-08 from the ApJ machine-readable file: Fimbulthul = stream 54 with 3724 stars (29 with VHel); Fimbulthul-S = stream 55 with 1734 stars (25 VHel), which the paper also interprets as omega Cen trailing debris lost 0.5-1 Gyr ago at ~3 kpc. The '22 members' figure from the Codex pass is wrong.

docs.title: Fitting campaign: omega Cen's stream in a barred Milky Way, then the DM test (plan, 2026-10-08)
docs.text:
Historical (2026-10-08)

Superseded; current status: kb/stream_status.md. Stages 0-2 ran from 2026-10-09. The Gaussian track objective planned below was replaced by the conditional per-star score, which was later found to disagree with it. The bar-angle prior and range below are superseded by the 9-D emulator design (angle 10-35 deg).

Status: plan of 2026-10-08; stages 0-2 ran from 2026-10-09 (originally "plan, not started"). Inputs: STREAM_KNEE_INVESTIGATION.md (all tests so far) and the Codex literature pass codex_research_fit_campaign_2026-10-08.md (fallback web research; arXiv IDs checked against the arXiv API: two errors in that report -- Koposov+2019 Orphan is arXiv:1812.08172, not 1812.08192 (= Erkal+2019 LMC mass); the 2026 omega Cen spectroscopy paper is Kuzma et al., arXiv:2605.23474).

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
1. Find bar (and minimal host) parameters for which a model of omega Cen's tails reproduces the observed track of Ibata+2024 stream 54, including the knee: sky path, both PMs, relative distance and v_los vs position along the arm.
  2. At that fit, test whether the three DM cases (A none, B moderate, C 5x DM inside 200 pc) are distinguishable, with nuisance parameters refitted under each and calibrated on mocks.

Starting point (tested): a rotating Hunter+2024 bar steepens the pmdec gradient to the observed one (Omega_b = 33 follows the data to b = 37) and turns the sky track by about half of the observed ~10 deg; axisymmetric hosts fail.

docs.title: Design choices (my draft vs Codex; adopted)
docs.text: Item Adopted Why / source Path coordinate Galactic b along the northern arm (monotonic from the cluster, b = 15 -> 41) with a fixed omega-Cen-anchored stream frame for reporting Simple, curved-path-safe for this segment; Codex prefers a general curved-path estimator (TrackStream, Starkman+2023 arXiv:2212.00949) -- not needed while b is monotonic Data track Per b bin (2 deg): stream + broad-background mixture in l, pmra, pmdec with Gaia per-star covariances; block (spatial) bootstrap errors; CMD-shift distance-modulus track with a zero-point nuisance; v_los kept per star Erkal+2017 Pal 5 (arXiv:1609.01282), Koposov+2023 OC (arXiv:2211.04495) Density / counts Not used in the likelihood Unknown STREAMFINDER completeness (Codex; agreed) Selection bias (a) magnitude-cut variants (G < 19 / < 20); (b) independent Gaia selection along the arm (WSDB: sky window + broad PM/CMD window, no orbit templates) and compare ridges; (c) systematic floor if they differ STREAMFINDER template selection (Malhan & Ibata 2018) Fast generator AGAMA particle spray (Fardal+2015 arXiv:1410.1861 as in AGAMA's tutorial; Chen et al. 2025 arXiv:2408.01496 release model) in the time-dependent barred host; Jacobi radius/frequency from the host evaluated at each release time seconds per model (to be benchmarked) Validation generator Our prescribed-potential tracer runs (3.4 min axi / 6.5 min barred, 8 threads); already exist for Hunter axi and bars 33/37.5/41 Codex: spray accuracy (~10% in Chen et al. 2025 tests) not established for a massive, rotating cluster in a bar DM-aware generator Tracer runs only (sprays know only total mass and r_J) DM enters via the mass profile and release distribution Objective Gaussian track likelihood per bin: (y - m)^T (C_obs + C_model + C_sys)^-1 (y - m), model summaries built with identical frame, cuts, binning and error convolution Erkal+2019 arXiv:1812.08192; Koposov+2023 Optimiser coarse grid -> Nelder-Mead / CMA-ES with common random numbers -> small emcee only if needed Codex; brute-force MCMC on tracer runs is unaffordable

docs.title: Revision 2026-10-09 after the methods review (STREAM_FIT_METHODS_REVIEW.md)
docs.text:
• Model track: select trailing-arm particles by the sign of the Gibbons+2014 phase chi (accumulated r - r_prog since release) and, where needed, by release time; bin in b; per bin a local linear fit to particles gives the model value and its error of the mean (Erkal+2019, Koposov+2023); require sigma_sim < sigma_data/5 (sets the particle number).
  • Mask only bins where the MODEL is multi-valued in b (Koposov+2023 practice); never mask the observed knee.
  • Likelihood: Gaussian per bin and observable with sigma_data^2 + sigma_sim^2; no extra error floors unless the user approves.
  • Spray: AGAMA, moving progenitor potential = our model's mass profile (Gibbons+2014: progenitor gravity essential), pericentre-weighted release (Erkal+2019) or Chen et al. 2025; validated against the tracer runs. StreaMAX not used (bar not wired into its integrator, 2D-only track).
  • Optimiser: simplex/Nelder-Mead from many prior draws or dual annealing (likelihood discontinuous), then emcee if needed.
  • Report the pull on omega Cen's present-day 6D point (Dillamore+2022: it absorbs perturbations); mock calibration of the DM test.

docs.title: Decision 2026-10-09 (user): bar-angle prior
docs.text: The spray grid prefers small bar angles (16-20 deg) with a strong bar (1.2-1.6 x Hunter), but the gain over 24 deg is modest (Delta lnL ~ 0.5 per member). In the fit the bar angle gets a tighter, literature-based prior (published estimates ~25-30 deg; exact prior to be set from cited measurements) instead of running free; the residual freedom is to be absorbed by omega Cen's present-day phase space (catalogue priors) and host parameters, not by an implausible bar.

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
Stage 0 -- freeze the observables (data only, ~1 day of work, negligible CPU). bin/streams/measure_track.py: ridge + width + errors per b bin for l, pmra, pmdec; distance-modulus track (from stream54_cmd_distance.py); v_los per star. Variants: all members, G < 19, independent Gaia selection. Gate: the knee (l turn and PM steepening at b > 30) persists across variants. Stream 55 measured separately, not fitted yet.

Stage 1 -- spray generator and its validation (~0.5 day, minutes of CPU). src/ocen_dm/streams/spray.py (AGAMA, time-dependent host, Chen et al. 2025/Fardal release, release-time window 0-1 Gyr). Benchmark runtime. Validate against the existing tracer runs (Hunter axi, bars 33/37.5/41; model A): same summaries through the Stage-0 pipeline. Gate: spray ridges within the data errors of the tracer ridges, else calibrate the release parameters (mean offset, dispersions) against the tracer runs, or fall back to tracer runs on a coarse grid.

Stage 2 -- bar fit with sprays (hours of CPU, to be fixed after the benchmark). Free: Omega_b (25-50 km/s/kpc), bar angle (20-35 deg), bar amplitude (0.7-1.3 x Hunter), omega Cen 6D present-day point (Gaussian priors: gc_catalog_full.fits values and errors). Host axisymmetric part fixed (Hunter+2024). Constant pattern speed. Search: grid (~10 x 4 x 4 = 160 sprays) -> local optimisation -> uncertainty by emcee only if a basin is clear. Gate: chi^2/dof acceptable, residuals unstructured along b; knee reproduced in l AND PMs (reject PM-only fits).

Stage 3 -- robustness (hours). Host variants (halo flattening / disc mass, one parameter at a time), bar angle/strength degeneracies, selection variants from Stage 0; slowing bar only if constant-speed residuals are structured.

Stage 4 -- high-fidelity check (1-3 h, 8 threads). Tracer runs at the best fit and 2-4 posterior extremes (model A); compare with sprays and data.

Stage 5 -- DM test (tracer runs; ~3 x (1 + nuisance refits) runs, plus mocks). At the Stage-2/3 host, run A, B, C (fitted rotation), refit the omega Cen nuisance point per case (sprays to locate, tracer runs to evaluate), compare likelihoods; mocks from A, B and C with the data's sampling and errors to measure false-positive rate and power. Detection criterion (campaign choice): Delta ln L (or ln Z) > 4.6 AND correct recovery in >= 90% of mocks. C's DM profile is explicit (results/nbody/C_dm5x_shell/model_profiles.json); it is a fixed potential (no DM stripping), so it is an upper limit on the DM effect for that profile.

docs.title: Risks and arguments against
docs.text:
• One ~25-deg segment may not separate Omega_b, bar angle, bar strength and the omega Cen point: priors on the latter from Gaia are tight, but bar parameters may stay degenerate. Report the degeneracy; it does not block the DM test if the DM signal is orthogonal to it -- check with mocks.
  • The STREAMFINDER selection can shape the track; the independent Gaia selection (Stage 0b) is the check.
  • Particle spray may misplace debris for a massive cluster with internal rotation; Stage 1/4 cross-checks.
  • The DM signal so far appears only in counts (not used); if it does not appear in track/PM/width under the bar, the answer is "not detectable with this stream", which is a result.

docs.text: All launches announced with expected %CPU, threads and wall time, with options (OMP_NUM_THREADS). No live N-body. Results in the journal; this file updated at each gate.

docs.title: Lessons for omega Cen
docs.text:
1. Nobody fits a fold by unwrapping in general. Tracks are built in an along-stream coordinate in which the observed segment is single-valued; regions where the MODEL folds are masked (K23) or handled by a KDE (D22). Explicit ordering (G14 chi; release time) is used to pick one arm/wrap. For us: the observed northern arm is single-valued in b; on the model side select the trailing arm by the sign of chi (or by release side) and, if needed, by release time, then bin in b. The knee itself must NOT be masked: it is the signal. Mask only where the model is multi-valued in b.
  2. Model summary per bin/knot from a local linear fit to particles (E19, K23), with the model's error of the mean in the likelihood and enough particles that sigma_sim < sigma_data/5 (K23; C26b uses /3).
  3. Likelihood: Gaussian per bin and observable, sigma_data^2 + sigma_sim^2. Extra error floors (K23 sigma_nuis, C26b sigma_sys) are ad hoc systematics -> need the user's approval before use (project rule).
  4. Progenitor gravity in the spray is essential (G14 Fig. 3); omega Cen is massive (3-4e6 Msun) -- use our model's mass profile as the moving progenitor potential (already done in run_prescribed.py).
  5. Release history matters: G14 uniform in time, E19/K23 concentrated at pericentres; our tracer runs show pericentre- driven escape. Prefer pericentre-weighted release (or Chen et al. 2025 calibration) and validate against the tracer runs.
  6. A good track fit does not mean an unperturbed stream; the progenitor's present-day phase space absorbs perturbations (D22: best fit with arms swapped by Sgr; optimiser shifted distance 7.47 -> 7.27 kpc). Keep Gaia/catalogue priors on omega Cen's 6D point and report any pull.
  7. Weak perturbations are degenerate with none (D22 mocks): the DM test needs mock calibration (E19 and K23 had none).
  8. Likelihoods from particles are discontinuous (bins gain/lose particles): derivative-free optimisers with loose tolerance (D22), simplex from many prior draws (E19), common random numbers.
  9. StreaMAX is not usable as is for us: the rotating bar exists in potentials.py:297-333 but generate_stream calls the host acceleration without t (integrants.py:20,65,114), no composite host, 2D projected radius only, float32. AGAMA (our pipeline) already handles the time-dependent barred host; reuse the StreaMAX ideas (G14 ordering, model-noise gate), not the code.

docs.title: omega Cen tails vs Fimbulthul: DM cases, rotation, host, and the stream-54 "knee" (2026-10-08)
docs.text:
Historical (2026-10-08/09)

Restricted N-body stream experiments, before the particle-spray work. Current status: kb/stream_status.md. The "distance is not the explanation" conclusion below relied on the CMD-shift distance track, withdrawn on 2026-10-10 (literature/omega_cen_stream_distances_2026-10-10.md). The "next steps" were carried out: particle sprays were built from 2026-10-09.

Consolidated record of the stream experiments of 2026-10-08. Day-by-day detail and all numbers are in the project journal (local) (entries from "Scoping: restricted N-body tails" to "No published model shows the PM knee"). Plan and user decisions: STREAM_EXPERIMENTS_PLAN.md.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• No model reproduces the northern arm of Ibata+2024 stream 54 beyond b ~ 25-30 deg. In all 15 model variants (3 DM cases x {McMillan17, + fitted rotation, + maximal rotation, DB98 + rotation, DB98 + rotation in Ibata's frame}) the dense model arm lies on the less-negative pmra edge of the data already at b = 15-30, keeps shallow gradients beyond b = 30 (pmra -6..-10 vs -10..-20, pmdec -7..-8.5 vs -9..-12.5 at b = 35-40), and continues straight to b ~ 45 at l = -50..-60 instead of bending to l ~ -30..-45. v_los agrees (200-230 vs 190-225 km/s at b = 30-40).
  • DM content changes debris counts only (A no DM > C 5x DM inside 200 pc ~ B moderate DM), not the track or PM gradients. Rotation fitted to the observed rotation changes counts by 1-2 %; maximal rotation does not help. DB98 raises counts by 22-36 % and broadens the arm, no knee. Ibata's solar frame (R0 8.122, Vsun 232.24, d = 5.63 kpc) moves the DB98 pericentre from 1.62 to 2.24 kpc and lowers counts; no knee.
  • No published model shows the PM knee either. Ibata+2019 Fig. 1 plots PMs vs l only for the DR2 Fimbulthul arc (b ~ 35, l = -52..-32); their "knee" (l ~ -57, b ~ 20, Fig. 4b) is a sky feature near the cluster. Ibata+2024 excludes stream 54 from its fit; Zheng+2026 report stronger observed bending than in their and Ibata's simulations. The premise "Ibata reproduces the knee" (adopted mid-day) was wrong.

  • Distance is not the explanation (tested). [Withdrawn 2026-10-10: the CMD-shift track used here is the outlier against the literature; see the banner.] CMD-shift distances along stream 54 (bin/streams/stream54_cmd_distance.py, plots/stream54_cmd_distance.png) fall by 8-12% from b = 15-20 to b = 33-42, matching the model arm (13%); there is no ~30% distance step. The PM knee is therefore a tangential-velocity mismatch at the same distance (~90 km/s at b = 35-40). A perturber or extra cluster DM cannot supply this (cluster: <~13 km/s even with 10x DM at 1 kpc; a flyby needs ~5e8 Msun within ~0.3 kpc).

  • Chemistry supports membership. Gaia XP (Andrae+2023) [M/H] of bright members (G < 15.5, giants) in the knee (N 19, median -1.36), next to the cluster (N 16, -1.60) and stream 55 (N 18, -1.31) are consistent with omega Cen members at the same G (N 1163, -1.47; KS p 0.17-0.80). Fainter XP members are dominated by metal-rich foreground dwarfs everywhere. So the knee is most likely omega Cen debris on a track our models do not reproduce.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
All runs: massless star tracers (200k from each model's DF-sampled ICs, results/nbody/<model>/ics.npz) in a static host plus the satellite's prescribed (fixed) spherical potential moving on the point-mass orbit integrated back from today (bin/streams/run_prescribed.py). Stars with r_max(E) < 30 pc cannot escape and are counted only. ~3-4 min per run on 8-10 threads.

Model Mass profile A A_nodm no DM (stars + remnants) B B_dm_phot moderate DM (photometric stellar mass, M/N19 = 9 halo) C C_dm5x_shell B inside 63 pc; DM density 0.159 Msun/pc^3 at 63-200 pc (M_DM(<200 pc) 1.15e6 -> 5.73e6); B's star tracers

Validation (earlier the same day): the refit restricted runner (bin/streams/run_restricted.py, satellite potential refitted every 2 Myr from bound tracers, frozen core) agrees with the live pyfalcon run of A over 1.96 Gyr to 10 % in escape fraction and 3 % in debris dE/dLz (plots/streams_validation_A.png); the prescribed potential loses 12 % fewer stars.

docs.title: Rotation (src/ocen_dm/streams/rotation.py, bin/streams/fit_spin.py)
docs.text: Lynden-Bell flips: counter-rotating tracers have v_phi (about the spin axis) reversed with probability q(r_max) = q0 x^2/(1+x^2)/(1+(r_max/r_q)^2), x = r_max/r_1. E and |v| unchanged (max change 1e-13 km/s), so the spherical equilibrium is exact. Axis: Ibata+2019 (PA 12 deg E of N, pole 45 deg towards us); sense from our data: oMEGACat v_los maximal at PA 103 deg (east receding) -> pole sky PA 192; Gaia DR3 rotation N -> E (-0.285, -0.245, -0.193, -0.125, -0.039 mas/yr at 3-6, 6-10, 10-15, 15-25, 25-36 arcmin; bin/streams/measure_gaia_rotation.py) -> pole towards us. Joint fit to Gaia PM + oMEGACat LOS amplitudes: tilt 50 deg, q0 = 1, r_1 = 4 pc, r_q = 63 pc (all three models); chi2 PM 7-13 / 5 bins, LOS 60-63 / 20 bins (model 1.5-2 km/s high inside 2'). Rotation in the escape region (36-60'): ~1 km/s. Maximal rotation: q = 1 at all radii (results/streams/spin_max/).

docs.title: Corrections and pitfalls recorded
docs.text:
1. Bin/box medians misled twice. (a) Model arm medians in 5-deg bins were dragged by a broad low-pmra spray and wrongly "agreed" with the data at b < 30; the overlay shows the offset. (b) Medians of the few model tracers inside a hand-picked knee box (47-61 per model) were wrongly presented as a "model knee"; streams_knee_release_db98_rot_A_nodm.png shows only a sparse spray there. Rule: make the overlay before any comparison claim.
  2. Parallax-distance argument withdrawn: it assumed agreement at b < 30. Stream-54 absolute parallax at the cluster (0.25 mas) exceeds omega Cen's 0.184 by 0.065 mas; only relative trends are usable.
  3. Centre-orbit accuracy: AGAMA's default accuracy (1e-8) loses 5-12 pc in a 2-Gyr backward-forward round trip; run_prescribed.py, run_restricted.py and restricted.centre_orbit now use 1e-12. Irrelevant for arm morphology, but it broke the bound/unbound split in db98_ibata plots.
  4. Frame consistency: DB98 runs before the ibata19 frame used McMillan17's solar velocity (252 km/s) with a host of v_c(R0) = 222 km/s.
  5. Distance 5.43 vs 5.63 kpc is a 3.7 % effect on PMs: not a candidate explanation.

docs.title: Stream proper motions and the bar angle: renewed investigation
docs.text:
Historical (2026-10-13)

Current status: kb/stream_status.md. All ln L values on this page are the legacy score S2 (equal-weight chi bins, implied background widths; see kb/models/stream_likelihood_versions.md), at 32,000 release epochs (pilots at 8,000). They are not comparable with later scores.

The task is to reproduce the remaining stream-54 proper-motion structure and determine whether the apparent preference for a low bar angle survives joint refitting. This note will record findings, including negative results.

docs.title: First experiment: complete the nuisance refinement
docs.text:
The previous broad six-dimensional search found comparable maxima at 16 and 28 degrees, but was not locally refined. Other angle comparisons fixed distance, proper motions, or bar size. Those comparisons do not establish the profiled angle preference.

bin/streams/refine_bar_profiles.py refines both angles with the original conditional score. Pattern speed, amplitude, bar size, cluster distance, and both cluster proper motions move together. Coordinates are scaled before bounded COBYQA optimization. The initial candidates include the best saved Sobol points and the best relevant grid models. Every evaluation and spray is saved; the result file is replaced atomically. Existing output is preserved.

The distance measurement is 5.43 +/- 0.05 kpc, and each PM measurement has an uncertainty of 0.027 mas/yr. These are separate penalty terms. Bar length is bounded by corotation using the measured Hunter A2 half-maximum length of 4.25 kpc. The 5 kpc definition remains an option. Bounds and measurements are recorded in the output. There is no new angular prior or error inflation.

The search uses 8,000 release epochs and seed 1. Candidate improvement will be checked at 32,000 epochs with independent seeds 4, 5, and 6. Comparisons are made only at equal particle count. This is a diagnostic refinement; an optimization budget ending before convergence is reported as such, and held-out seed checks do not substitute for mock calibration.

CPU limit approved by the user: two cores. Run each angle in a separate single-thread process, with BLAS also limited to one thread. Expected first refinement runtime: 15-30 minutes, to be updated from measured timings.

docs.title: Interpretation requirements
docs.text:
A better raw score is insufficient. Compare the actual sky and PM tracks, the remaining PM residuals, the external distance/PM tension, the nuisance boundaries, and scores from independent seeds. Keep the near-cluster and distal segments visible. Do not claim that a prior forcing a normal bar angle has explained the low-angle preference.

Possible further diagnostics include projecting PM residuals along and across the measured sky track and testing whether the stars with radial velocities can reach physically plausible escape locations in the barred host. These are distinct from comparing a star orbit with the cluster orbit using arbitrary position/velocity scales.

docs.title: PM geometry diagnostic
docs.text:
bin/streams/diagnose_pm_profiles.py predicts PMs with particles weighted only by their agreement with each member's sky position. It retains the existing chi-bin weights, and never uses an observed PM to select a model particle. The diagnostic plot uses a declared two-degree tube around the measured ridge; the fit still uses all members. Each bin records its member count and model PM/distance percentiles. This avoids attributing a change in broad distribution shape to a shift of the ridge.

The initial diagnostic, before the local fits finished, suggests two different errors. Around phi1=11-17 degrees, the PM vector direction differs by several degrees. At the distal knee, phi1=23-27, the vector direction is much closer, but its magnitude is too small. A purely local distance rescaling at fixed relative space velocity would remove most of that distal PM residual. This is a decomposition of the error, not a measured distance or a new freedom in the dynamical model: changing the actual cluster distance also changes the orbit, and must be forward-modelled.

docs.title: Separate physical hypothesis: spiral arms
docs.text:
The stream host omits the spiral potential supplied with the local Hunter model. The published model contains independently rotating bar and spiral patterns. The reference spiral speed is 22.5 km/s/kpc and the reported test range is 17.5-25. The original setup uses both components at phase -25 degrees today, in a frame with Sun at negative x.

Sources: Hunter et al. 2024, Sections 2.1.6 and 2.2.2, and the authors' AGAMA implementation. The local exported potential and construction script are the numerical inputs; they are not assumed to equal every parameter in the published text.

src/ocen_dm/streams/spiral.py reflects the exported CylSpline tables into this project's x_model=-x_source frame by applying the exact real-Fourier parity to potential and derivative coefficients. It then adds independent positive pattern rotation. A sign change of pattern speed alone would leave the spiral winding wrong. Original and transformed hashes are saved under results/streams/spiral_potential/.

bin/streams/diagnose_spiral_forcing.py check verifies force/potential reflection, zero-amplitude identity, force addition, and past/present phase. The reflection force error is 9.5e-16 relative to the largest checked spiral force. Phase/addition errors are below 4e-14. The source has a numerical azimuthal-monopole remainder of 1.17e-7 of the spiral potential amplitude; reflection preserves it to 8e-17. An initial absolute-zero threshold rejected that source remainder; the check now verifies preservation of the source monopole explicitly. No measured-data errors or likelihood widths changed.

The pilot is a paired on/off experiment at fixed cluster/bar parameters, fixed present spiral phase 25 degrees, and a fresh spray seed. A source snapshot is frozen before each pilot. A gain in one seed is only a lead: check the PM tracks, independent seeds, and nuisance refitting before interpreting it as an explanation for the angle preference.

docs.title: First numerical findings
docs.text:
The exploratory local searches were stopped after 19 evaluations at 16 degrees and 28 at 28, when an independent 8,000-epoch seed shift exceeded the residual angle gap. They are not converged profile maxima. Their checkpoints and every evaluated spray remain available. Three independent 32,000-epoch sprays (seeds 4, 5, 6) were run for each selected candidate and its initial reference.

Angle Initial mean ln L Refined mean ln L Gain 16 deg -22394.7 -22178.6 +216.1 28 deg -22957.9 -22463.6 +494.3

The paired 16-minus-28 differences are 314.5, 172.4, and 368.1: mean 285.0, seed scatter 101.0. These quantify simulation noise at two candidates; they are not observational errors or a significance for the bar angle. The 28-degree candidate compensates with D=5.801 kpc and pmdec=-6.8256 mas/yr, near the imposed -3-sigma PM boundary. Its distance is 7.4 sigma above the adopted 5.43 +/- 0.05 measurement (2.5 sigma under the older stream prior of +/- 0.15). This is unresolved external-measurement tension, not a successful removal of the angle problem.

The fixed-parameter spiral pilot at 28 degrees, seed 4, improves ln L by 277.1 (fiducial) or 317.2 (fast), versus 41.0 for the slow pattern. The gain is mostly distal. Its sky-conditioned PMDEC shifts are only about 0.1-0.25 mas/yr; a 1-2 mas/yr residual remains in the distal bins. This pilot does not solve either requested problem and still needs denser, independent seeds before treating its gain as reliable.

docs.title: Likelihood density audit
docs.text:
Writing the implemented score as

L(w|u) = pi(u) [f(u,w)/f_u(u)] + [1-pi(u)] g_w(w)

gives pi(u) = (1-eps) f_u / [(1-eps) f_u + eps g_u]. The foreground conditional is density-free, but its mixture weight is not. This is an intentional coverage behavior in the original formula and should not be described as complete independence from the model's along-stream density.

bin/streams/audit_conditional_density.py isolates that dependency by rescoring with a fixed conditional mixing weight, while retaining all kernels and background constants. Production scoring is unchanged; return_components=True only exposes densities for this audit. Every saved validation/pilot score replays with zero difference.

The change does not remove the low-angle ranking. In the original 56-candidate grid the best 28-degree deficit changes from 1447.3 to 1443.9. In the independent refined candidates it strengthens the average 16-degree advantage from 285.0 to about 392.0. The density mixing issue is real, but is not an explanation of the angle preference in these tests. The original background-support normalization issue remains separate. (Update: fixed on 2026-10-17, score version S3; see kb/models/stream_likelihood_versions.md.)

docs.title: RV-star connection diagnostic
docs.text:
bin/streams/backtrack_barred_release.py integrates the RV stars backward in the actual fitted barred host plus the moving progenitor potential. It scans distances and compares encounters in units of the model's time-dependent tidal radius and release velocity. Model stars chosen by sky position provide a reference check. It includes a small number of observable-error draws, and records edge hits. This is a diagnostic at two fitted states, not a complete ancestry exclusion or posterior.

This addresses a question the earlier axisymmetric backtrack could not: whether the measured PM/RV combinations can originate near the cluster in the model that is actually being fitted, rather than whether another optimizer can improve an uncalibrated scalar score.

Completed: 29 RV stars plus 29 sky-matched model controls at each angle. For phi1<17, the median nominal encounter diagnostic is 0.80 for the data at either angle, versus 1.05/0.99 for model controls. For the 13 knee RV stars, data medians are 1.99/1.86 at 16/28 degrees, versus 1.11/1.13 for controls. Selecting the best of four small observational-error draws gives 1.96/1.76 for the knee data. Some distal stars have relative velocities of several release-velocity scales even at their best encounter.

This identifies a physical mismatch in the tested recent fixed-potential models beyond the scoring choice. It does not exclude ancestry: the distance grid is coarse, error sampling is sparse, only two cluster states/bar histories are tested, and the encounter metric is not a release likelihood.

docs.title: Escape-law pilot
docs.text:
Run at 8,000 release epochs, seed 4, legacy score S2 (results/plot_data/escape_pilot_20261013/).

The current Fardal/Gala release has zero relative radial motion. Its implementation matches the local AGAMA tutorial, so this is not a sign or transcription bug. Chen et al. 2025 provide a calibrated alternative with radial escape motion, correlated escape radius/direction, and integration in the progenitor potential. The code uses their five-dimensional Gaussian prescription and the actual spherical satellite escape speed. This is a controlled alternative; Chen's tests do not certify it for Omega Cen's massive, central, barred orbit.

src/ocen_dm/streams/escape.py implements the new prescription. The Fardal default is bitwise identical to the committed reference; Chen isolated escape energies close to zero to 2.8e-15 relative precision, and sample moments/correlation agree with the stated parameters. Spin is not silently added to the new calibrated prescription.

bin/streams/compare_escape_recipes.py makes a paired comparison of release law and launch-arm selection. Both launch arms can contribute positive Gibbons chi after integration, so filtering on the initial outer-arm label is an additional assumption. The four pilot cases isolate these effects; the old default is preserved. All bar/cluster parameters and likelihood kernels stay fixed; new-case metadata and source hashes are recorded.

The fixed-state, seed-4 pilot does not fix the mismatch. At 28 degrees, Fardal -> Chen increases the sky-conditioned PM-ridge RMS from 1.44 to 1.51 mas/yr and lowers ln L by 465. Including both launch arms adds about 200 positive-chi particles to Fardal (~4%) and only 50 to Chen; its score changes are small and its PM shifts do not resolve the residual. The outer-arm subset from the both-arm Fardal run matches the default in every saved observable and chi/age array exactly. These are tests at frozen Fardal-fitted states, not a rejection of every refitted Chen model.

Next connection controls: extend the backward interval to 2 Gyr while retaining the same present state/potential. The 700 Myr foreground cut is a modelling assumption, not an age measurement for the mismatched knee. If needed, the script also supports the existing slowing-bar prescription and the actual catalogue cluster state, with independently generated model controls. These are distinct tests, not a change to the active likelihood.

Update: the 2 Gyr backward run exists (results/plot_data/bar_profile_refinement_20261013/barred_backtrack_an{16,28}_b2000.json) but was never analysed.

docs.title: What the omega Cen stream (stream 54) requires to be fitted well
docs.text: Status: 2026-10-22. Summary figure: plots/stream_requirements.png (bin/streams/requirements_figure.py).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• A good fit needs a non-axisymmetric force at R = 4-7 kpc about 2.5-3.5 times that of the published Milky Way bar, locked to the bar (co-rotating, in phase). With the bar's strength and size free, every good fit inflates the Hunter+2024 / Sormani+2022 bar to amplitude A ~ 1.4 and size S ~ 1.25-1.33. Its quadrupole is then ~2.6-3.2 times the published one; inside 3 kpc the increase is only 1.2-1.4 times (panel a).
  • With the bar fixed at its published strength, size and angle (27 deg), the best fit is 2,627 worse in ln L than the best inflated-bar fit, and even that needs an ultrafast bar (Omega_b = 44.8 km/s/kpc; panels b, c). The failure is mainly mu_alpha* in the middle of the stream, where the model is 1-3 mas/yr too negative at phi1 7-19 deg: the PM turn starts too early.
  • The stream measures a torque history, not a static force. Along omega Cen's orbit the extra force averages to zero (<= 0.003 |F_axi| over 300-700 Myr) but its rms is about 2x the published bar's. omega Cen's L_z swings more widely (panel d), and the 300-700-Myr-old debris records that history. No axisymmetric change (disc, halo flattening, v_c, solar frame, distance, PMs) can replace it.
  • Within the inflated-bar model the stream prefers a low bar angle (12.5-17.5 deg; 25 deg is 1,071 worse, 27.5 deg 1,885 worse). The preference survives every test below. It is conditional on the inflated bar.
  • The demanded bar conflicts with local constraints: its m=2 strength at the solar radius is 0.062 |F_axi|, against 0.01-0.02 in Hercules/OLR models. Equivalently, the long bar would need to be ~2x as massive as Sormani+2022's (total bar ~2.4e10 vs 1.83e10 Msun) and ~1.3x longer, reaching corotation (~6.4 kpc, against 5.0 +- 0.2 kpc measured).

docs.title: Model and data
docs.text:
• Members: STREAMFINDER (Ibata+2024) stream 54 within the stream's footprint; Gaia DR3 PMs with covariances; 29 v_los.
  • Model: Fardal-type particle spray from omega Cen in the Hunter+2024 barred Milky Way. The bar is A x [baryon_full(x/S) - baryon_axi(x/S)] rotating at Omega_b; the axisymmetric part uses an Einasto halo with flattening q, normalised to v_c(R0).
  • Frame and priors: gravity21 solar frame (R0 8.275 kpc, Sgr A* PM, z_sun 20.8 pc). omega Cen's distance is held in 5.33-5.53 kpc, with priors on the distance, systemic PMs and v_c (233 +- 7 km/s).
  • Score: conditional likelihood p(Delta phi2, PMs, v_los | phi1) with fixed chi bins 0-200, jackknife-corrected; debris younger than 700 Myr.
  • Parameters (9): bar angle, Omega_b, A, S, d, mu_alpha*, mu_delta, v_c, q.
  • Statistics: the score is overconfident by T ~ 2 (calibrated on 20 mock catalogues, bin/streams/tempering_calibration.py). The star bootstrap gives the right sampling errors; the block bootstrap overstates them 2-6x. Statistical sd of angle-to-angle differences is ~30-80 in ln L.

docs.title: What the stream does not require (tested and ruled out as substitutes)
docs.text:
• An axisymmetric change: these cannot mimic a torque history. Halo flattening and disc mass were tested on 10-10 and all made the fit worse; disc_scale was not refitted in the current setup.
  • Spiral arms at the published amplitude.
  • A slowing bar (tested on 10-10 in the old frame: worse at every pattern speed).
  • A release-history change (pericentric bursts).
  • A selection effect: the Gaia search finds no off-track debris.

docs.title: Remaining misfits, common to every model tried
docs.text:
• Delta phi2 offsets: -1.2 to -2 deg at phi1 3-15 and +1.2 to +2.3 deg at 25-27 deg.
  • Knee mu_delta 0.5-1 mas/yr too shallow (phi1 > 19); knee debris 7-10% too close against the CMD distance track.
  • Fit pulled to range edges: distance at the band top (5.52-5.53 kpc), v_c 223-226 km/s.
  • Along-stream density: the members' ~10x gap at phi1 6-13 is not reproduced (the score does not use the density).

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text: The stream constrains a bar-locked, non-axisymmetric force history along omega Cen's retrograde orbit (pericentre 1.5-2 kpc, apocentre 6.4-7.2 kpc) more firmly than it constrains the bar angle. Within the Hunter bar family this force comes out ~2x the published bar's outer force; with it, the angle is low (~12-18 deg). The published bar cannot fit the stream at any pattern speed in 20-50. The most physical candidate not yet tested is a co-rotating "dark bar", the halo's response to the stellar bar (Petersen+2016), which extends beyond the stellar bar. Whether it can supply the force without violating the solar-neighbourhood constraints is open.

docs.title: Statistical vs systematic uncertainty
docs.text: With T ~ 2 the formal (statistical) errors are tiny: angle ~0.3-1 deg, Omega_b ~0.1, A ~0.02. The posterior's 68% region spans Delta lnL ~ 10, below the simulation noise (sd 14-35 at 256k). Model changes move the best fit 50-500 times further, so the uncertainty is systematic and is represented by the spread between model variants. A Laplace covariance for the final model is planned once the model is settled (docs/reviews/fable_posterior_revisited_20261022.md).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
1. A co-rotating dark-bar (halo-wake) component as the physical source of the extra force.
  2. A Hercules / solar-neighbourhood check of the demanded bar (U-V distribution with test particles, against Gaia).
  3. With the final model: a Laplace covariance, and per-segment residuals.

docs.title: Stream 54: status (2026-10-18)
docs.text: This page summarises the stream work since 2026-10-13. Earlier results are on the PM refinement page (historical). Every ln L below names its score version and particle number. Totals from different versions or particle numbers are not comparable; the versions are defined on stream likelihood versions.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• A bar is needed, but the fit is not yet satisfactory. Barred models beat the best axisymmetric model by about 3300–4100 in ln L. No model reproduces the steep μδ of the turn at φ1 > 22°.
  • Two objectives disagree. Fits to the binned tracks halve the track χ2 but lose 100–450 in the star-by-star ln L. The disagreement is a trade-off between the sky track and the PM track in the turn.
  • The original likelihood did not converge with particle number. It is replaced by fixed χ bins with equal weights. A jackknife removes the small-particle-number bias.
  • A 9-parameter emulator is built and validated (470 sprays). It does not yet constrain the bar. One independently checked point beats the paper models by about 600, but the turn is still not fitted.

docs.title: Model comparison
docs.text:
Scores S2 (2026-10-16) and S3 (2026-10-17), 32,000 release epochs. The host is the Hunter+2024 Milky Way (2024A&A...692A.216H); the axisymmetric null uses the same host with bar amplitude 0.

Model Δln L vs refined 16° bar, S2 (seeds 4–6) ln L, S3 (seed 4) Refined 16° bar 0 −22552.5 Refined 28° bar −292 ± 157 −22946.9 Axisymmetric null, ω Cen distance and PMs refitted −3541 ± 196 −26649.3 Axisymmetric null, catalogue state −7565 ± 86 —
  • Columns. Δln L: mean and seed scatter over three seeds. S3 differs from S2 only in the normalisation of the uniform background; the ranking is unchanged (16° − 28°: +321 in S2 and +394 in S3 at seed 4).
  • The refitted null runs to the bounds: distance 5.95 kpc (10.4σ from the adopted 5.43 ± 0.05 kpc), PMs 2.6–3.0σ off.
  • Host variants of the null (halo flattening 0.8/1.2, disc scale 0.8/1.2, vc(R0) 220/240 km s−1, McMillan 2017) change ln L by −630 to +370. All remain 3300–4300 below the 16° bar, and none steepens μδ in the turn (−8.3 to −9.0 mas yr−1 at φ1 = 25°, against −11.0 in the data).
  • Barred residuals. μδ is too shallow by 0.8 mas yr−1 at φ1 = 21° and by 1.2–1.8 at 23–27°. Most of the barred gain over the null (about 2900 of 3250–3550) comes from φ1 > 17°.
  • The 16° vs 28° gap shrinks with particle number. Under the pooled score the 28° − 16° difference is −454 at 4,000 epochs and −98 ± 18 at 512,000 (five seeds), and still trending towards zero. The bar angle is therefore not yet constrained by these comparisons.

docs.title: Track objective vs star-by-star likelihood
docs.text:
Fits to binned tracks (Δφ2 and PM medians in 2° bins of φ1; bin/streams/fit_track_objective.py) roughly halve the track χ2 of the refined models. Scored star by star (S2, 32,000 epochs, seeds 5 and 6) they are 100–450 worse in ln L.

The disagreement comes from the turn (bin/streams/plot_objective_disagreement.py):

  • the track-optimised long bar matches the PM medians to φ1 ≈ 25° but puts the turn debris 1.5° below the members in Δφ2 at φ1 = 21–26°;
  • the refined 28° bar has the sky track right at φ1 = 18–24° but PMs that are too shallow.

No model found so far gets both. Separately, all barred models place the young debris near the cluster about 1° from the observed track at φ1 = 2–8°; the axisymmetric null does not.

docs.title: Likelihood: convergence, bias and noise
docs.text:
• Legacy score (S2/S3) does not converge. It gives every χ bin with at least 20 particles equal weight, so the number of bins grows with particle number. Model differences changed sign between 4,000 and 128,000 epochs.
  • Fixed χ bins (chosen 2026-10-17). Bins of width 5 with fixed edges and equal weights, empty bins kept. Equal weight per χ interval keeps the model's density along the stream out of the score, because that density is not reliably modelled. The candidate range is χ = 0–200, which holds 93–96% of the model debris inside the data window; no member loses more than 2 in ln L against the pooled score. The library default is still the pooled score until this range is confirmed.
  • Noise is shot noise. The seed variance of each member's ln L follows 1/neff, the effective number of model particles behind its density, for neff ≳ 3. Neighbouring members share particles, so the noise of the total is 2–3 times the independent-star value. Members with few particles sit in the far turn (φ1 > 22°).
  • Bias: corrected with a jackknife. The log of a noisy density is biased low, by about 45–140 at 256,000 epochs depending on the parameters. A delete-group jackknife (10 interleaved groups; src/ocen_dm/streams/score_bias.py) removes it:
Calibration point Raw: 256k − 128k Jackknife: 256k − 128k Seed sd at 128k / 256k 14 (near the centre of the design) +73 ± 34 −10 ± 35 85 / 43 20 (largest bar amplitude × size) +25 ± 27 −5 ± 32 62 / 43

Means and seed scatter over 8 independent seeds per resolution, fixed χ bins 0–200. The check is limited to about ±35 by the number of seeds. A second-order (delta-method) correction removes only about half the bias.

docs.title: Emulator (2026-10-18)
docs.text:
Data. 470 sprays at 256,000 release epochs over 375 points of the 9-parameter space (bin/streams/training_set.py, bin/streams/stream_batch.py), each scored with fixed χ bins 0–200 and jackknife-corrected: - 256 Sobol design points; - 32 points with two extra independent seeds, for the noise. Each repeat shifts the release-time grid by a random offset as well as redrawing the escape offsets; the original runs agree with the shifted repeats (mean difference −24 ± 20); - two refinement rounds (100 and 60 runs) chosen by predicted ln L + 2σ, with exploration points, held-out points and repeats; - 8 seeds at the emulator maximum.

Model. Stochastic kriging (src/ocen_dm/streams/emulator.py; Ankenman, Nelson & Staum 2010, 2010OpRes..58..371A; Binois, Gramacy & Ludkovski, arXiv:1611.05902): - a GP for the mean, with each point's noise fixed; - a noise surface ln s² = a + b ln vjk + GP fitted to the repeat variances (median noise sd 65 in ln L).

Validation (5-fold, noise model refitted in each fold; results/plot_data/emulator_validate_final_20261018.json):

Subset RMSE Bias (true − predicted) z sd 95 % coverage All 375 points 1269 −76 1.08 0.94 Top 20 % 1043 +467 0.95 0.95 18 held-out points (never fitted) 1123 −413 1.01 16/18
  • Columns. z = (measured − predicted)/total predicted sd. The uncertainties are roughly right overall but not yet established near the maximum: the top quintile is biased by +467 and only 18 points were held out.

Results. - The bar is not yet constrained. The emulator's uncertainty is about 575 at the profile peaks and 806 at its optimised maximum, while each one-parameter profile (maximum over the other eight) varies by only 500–1350. Profiles are maxima over a finite candidate set with pointwise bands, not uncertainty-integrated. The emulator maximum moves between fits. - The two paper models are indistinguishable at current precision: 16° −22174 and 28° −22171 (2 seeds each; difference 3 ± ~70). They also differ in distance, amplitude and size, so this is not a clean test of the angle. - One independently replicated point is about 600 better: −21569 ± 11 (8 seeds) at angle 17°, Ωb 32, amplitude 1.57, size 0.89, distance 5.79 kpc, vc 220 km s−1, q 1.02. Its slow bar, large distance and low vc describe this candidate, not a measurement. The score has no prior on ω Cen's distance (adopted 5.43 ± 0.05 kpc). vc sits at the lower edge of the range; the latest emulator maximum also sits at the edges of μδ and halo q. - Predicted maxima are optimistic. The three checked predicted-best points came in 430–770 below their predictions. - The turn is still not fitted. At φ1 = 21° the best point improves the μδ residual from −0.82 to −0.16 mas yr−1 (paper 16°), but its Δφ2 offset grows from 0.47° to 1.42°. This is a remaining mismatch, not shown to be unavoidable everywhere in the space.

Open decisions: 1. extend vc below 220 km s−1 (and check the μδ and halo-q edges); 2. add the distance measurement as a prior or keep the score likelihood-only; 3. denser local design around the top (a local GP is an experiment), keeping global exploration and fresh held-out points; 4. choose the tempering by held-out segments and mock coverage.

docs.title: Frames and host variants (stream models)
docs.text:
These are fixed inputs of every stream spray, set in code rather than read from data files.

  • Solar frames (src/ocen_dm/streams/frames.py, FRAMES):
Frame R0 (kpc) z⊙ (pc) V⊙ (km/s) ω Cen distance (kpc) baumgardt (default) 8.178 0 (11.1, 252.24, 7.25) 5.43 (cluster.OCEN_DISTANCE_KPC) ibata19 (Ibata+2019 host) 8.122 17 (11.1, 232.24, 7.25) 5.63

V⊙ is astropy's galcen_v_sun. The model (AGAMA) frame flips the sign of x and vx relative to astropy's Galactocentric frame. - Cluster reference state (src/ocen_dm/cluster.py, since 2026-10-16): centre (201.69683333, −47.47956944) deg; systemic PM (−3.250, −6.746) ± 0.022 mas/yr; vlos 232.7 ± 0.2 km/s; distance 5.43 ± 0.05 kpc. Sources are on the cluster data page (L3). Runs before 2026-10-16 started from the Baumgardt orbit-table state, which differs by 0.04″ in position, 10⁻⁴ mas/yr in PM and 0.08 km/s in vlos (frames.py docstring). - Axisymmetric host variants (src/ocen_dm/streams/mw_variants.py, axisymmetric_variant). The Hunter+2024 axisymmetric baryons (MWPotentialHunter24_baryon_axi.ini) plus its dark halo, with: - halo flattening q (halo_q, axisRatioZ); - disc scale (disc_scale), which adds (scale − 1) × the thin and thick stellar discs; - vc(R0 = 8.178 kpc) set through the halo normalisation: kept at the original model's value by default, or set to vc_target.

The bar's non-axisymmetric part, A × (baryon_full − baryon_axi), is added unchanged. - LMC (src/ocen_dm/streams/lmc.py). Rigid MW and rigid LMC on their mutual orbit, following Vasiliev, Belokurov & Erkal 2021 (Sect. 3.1), without halo deformation. Particles are integrated in the MW-centred frame with the reflex acceleration, so only the tidal LMC field acts. The LMC is a truncated NFW with rs = 8.5 (M/10¹¹ M⊙)0.6 kpc, cut off at 10 rs; default mass 1.5×10¹¹ M⊙ (with_lmc). Dynamical friction acts on the LMC only. Present-day LMC: ICRS (81.0, −69.75) deg, PM (1.8, 0.35) mas/yr, d = 50 kpc, vlos = 260 km/s. - Bar size limit (bin/streams/training_set.py). Size S scales the Hunter+2024 bar; at S = 1 its length is Rbar = 4.25 kpc (the A2 half-peak length; RBAR_KPC). In the emulator design S runs from 0.8 to min(1.5, RCR/4.25 kpc), so the bar never extends beyond corotation RCR of that point's axisymmetric host. - Stream background box. The uniform background of the stream likelihood is normalised over an explicit box (Δφ2 −10 to 23 deg) since score S3; see stream likelihood versions.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text: STREAMFINDER (Ibata+2024) stream 54: 3,724 members on the sky (colour: G), of which the stream models are fitted to the 3,681 inside the load_data cut (b > 15°, −75° < l < −20°; bin/streams/spray_bar_grid2.py); proper motions along the stream in the chord great-circle frame φ1, showing the steepening beyond φ1 ≈ 15° (the "knee"); and the 29 radial velocities.

docs.text:
• Source (configs/data.yaml:50–61). ApJ 967, 89; arXiv:2311.17202; ADS 2024ApJ...967...89I. Table 1 is the MRT apjad382dt1_mrt.txt from content.cld.iop.org (not on VizieR). Fetched 2026-10-08; the MRT sha256 is 76742daa….
  • Files.
  • CAT/streamfinder_ibata2024_dr3_mrt.txt (2,432,198 B): the registered path.
  • CAT/streamfinder_ibata2024_dr3.fits (2,364,480 B): what the code reads. No conversion script and no checksum exist for it.
  • Contents. 24,540 rows.
  • Stream 54 (Fimbulthul): 3,724 stars, 29 with VHel.
  • Stream 55 (Fimbulthul-S): 1,734 stars, 25 with VHel.
  • e_VHel = 300 means null.
  • Loader. bin/streams/spray_bar_grid2.py:24–32 load_data.
  • Keeps Stream == 54 with b > 15° and −75° < l < −20°: 3,681 of the 3,724 members.
  • Sets VHel to NaN unless e_VHel < 300.
  • Attaches S2 errors and correlations.
  • About 20 scripts import it (fit_bar_ocen.py, grid4_common.py → grid4, fit_lmc_ocen, rescore_* and others). About 15 more read the FITS directly with the same cut.
  • Scoring. src/ocen_dm/streams/score.py.
  • Restrictions.
  • Track-only (STREAMFINDER selection, as for T4).
  • Ibata+2024 exclude stream 54 from their own potential fit (the project journal).
  • Member parallaxes are biased by +0.063 mas relative to the cluster (the project journal).
  • Status. c.

docs.title: Stream likelihood versions
docs.text:
Every stream ln L quoted in the journal, the plots or the paper was computed with one of the score versions below. Numbers from different versions are not comparable. The stream results index assigns each saved result file to a version, the script that wrote it, its non-default score options, its spray settings (particle number, seeds, frame, host options) and the code commit (generated by bin/streams/score_provenance.py from bin/streams/score_registry.py, a code audit of all 51 scripts that call a stream score, 2026-10-17).

From 2026-10-17 every call to grid4_common.score() returns settings (version tag, explicit options, code commit, -dirty if the score code had uncommitted changes); scripts that save scores should store it with their results.

Status (2026-10-17)

  • Chosen: fixed chi bins. The user chose fixed chi bins (equal weight per chi interval; candidate range 0-200 in steps of 5, i.e. chi_edges=np.arange(0., 205., 5.)) over the pooled KDE, because the density along the stream is not modelled reliably. Pooling weights each part of the stream by its debris fraction and so reintroduces that dependence (Codex review of the score provenance).
  • Default not yet changed. grid4_common.score() still defaults to pooled=True (S4-pooled) until the chi range is fixed.
  • Bias correction is not a score version. The jackknife correction of the particle-number bias (src/ocen_dm/streams/score_bias.py, commits 87771f5 and e6c4dc8) is applied to the scores after scoring.
  • Overall stream status: stream status.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
tag from commit (date) function what changed S0 89b1473 (2026-10-09 01:24) score per-star sky-conditional score S1 7183e33 (2026-10-09 06:20) score_chi_kde chi-binned KDE with latent chi; capped bandwidths from b5598ca S2 29d04f8 (2026-10-09 14:01) score_conditional conditional p(w | u) chi-KDE; equal-weight chi bins; background widths implied S3 ff312ad (2026-10-17 06:51) score_conditional as S2, uniform background normalised over an explicit box containing every member S4-pooled 899d5e5 (2026-10-17 13:54) score_conditional as S3, one KDE of all debris (no chi bins)

Results from before S0 (until 2026-10-09 01:24) did not use a per-star likelihood (track comparisons, validation checks).

docs.title: Settings common to S2-S4
docs.text:
Fixed since 29d04f8 (checked against the function signature at every later commit that touched the score):

  • kernels: h_u = h_x = 0.5 deg (along / across the stream in the chord great-circle frame), PMs 0.2 mas/yr added to each member's Gaia covariance, v_los 5 km/s added to the measurement error;
  • background fraction eps = 0.05; release-age cut 700 Myr; trailing-arm particles with chi > 0;
  • chi bins (S2, S3 only): width 5, minimum 20 particles, each kept bin weight 1/K;
  • background: S2 widths 12 deg (Delta phi2) x 30 x 30 mas/yr x 400 km/s; S3 onwards the box BG_BOUNDS / V_BOUNDS in bin/streams/grid4_common.py (Delta phi2 -10..23 deg; PMs and v_los unchanged);
  • data: stream-54 members and frame results/plot_data/stream54_gc_frame_chord.json, along-stream window = member range.

docs.title: Replaying a version
docs.text:
version call S2 score(m, legacy_background=True) S3 score(m, legacy_bins=True) S4-pooled score(m) S4-chi_edges score(m, chi_edges=np.arange(0., 205., 5.))

S0 and S1 need a checkout of their commit.

docs.title: Inputs that changed independently of the score
docs.text:
• Cluster reference state (9601ba7, 2026-10-16 07:29): one source for omega Cen's position, PMs, distance and v_los (v_los 232.78 -> 232.7 km/s, PMs at 1e-4). Sprays made before and after differ at the ~10-20 ln L level, below the seed scatter. The refined bar fits (2026-10-13) predate it; the paper models (2026-10-16) were re-sprayed after it.
  • Spray speed-ups (dfc3d78, 2026-10-11): trailing arm only and the 700 Myr cut; bit-identical output (tests).
  • Chunked orbit integration (2026-10-17): memory only; bit-identical output (test).
  • Particle number and seeds: in the results index (from the code) and, partly, in each results file. Totals depend on them (shot-noise bias of ln of a KDE, which grows as the particle number falls); compare models only at equal particle number.

docs.title: Known inconsistencies (audit 2026-10-17)
docs.text:
• Scripts that call score_conditional directly (grid4.py, kernel_check.py, d2_mock_recovery.py, rescore_conditional.py, knee_spread_and_frame.py, fit_bar_ocen.py --conditional) always compute S2, whatever the wrapper default.
  • obs_split.single_scores (per-observable scores in d1_segments.py, mass_sweep.py, cluster_mass_test.py, frame_obs_split.py) and the plotting re-implementations (plot_conditional_model.py, plot_conditional_orig.py) hard-code S2. Next to a wrapper score from S3 onwards, the two columns use different definitions.
  • Resumable or appending outputs skip entries already present (paper_models.json, phase2_variants.json, phase2b_grid.json, profile_stage1.json, sun_dist_bar_grids.json, frame_decomp_edges.json, mass_sweep.json, cluster_mass_test.json, bar3d_sweep/, lmc_spray_test.jsonl, the refinement / spiral / escape pilot files, the convergence and n_eff studies). Resumed after a version change, they would hold mixed versions with no marker in the file.
  • d1_segments.py runs at import; knee_spread_and_frame.py imports it and so rewrites the D1 outputs.

docs.title: Distances to omega Cen stream (Fimbulthul) stars: literature (2026-10-10)
docs.text:
Research agent read full texts (arXiv PDFs); key quotes spot-checked by me in the extracted texts (Ibata+2019 Fig. 3a caption "offset by 0.7 magnitudes ... ~1.5 kpc closer than omega Cen"; Methods "mean distance to these stars of 4.1 kpc, as predicted by the STREAMFINDER algorithm"; Fig. 1 = 0.265 +- 0.008 mas; Ibata+2021 table note "column 9 provides the distance to the star dSF estimated by the algorithm").

  • No standard-candle or spectroscopic distance gradient exists along Fimbulthul. All along-stream distances come from STREAMFINDER: PARSEC SSP template (12.5 Gyr, fixed [Fe/H] per run) fitted to Gaia photometry; weak parallax term from Ibata+2021 (arXiv:2012.05245, Eq. 2). Authors note a distance-metallicity degeneracy and multiple distance solutions.
  • Ibata+2019 Nature Astronomy (arXiv:1902.09544): stream ~0.7 mag brighter than omega Cen in the CMD (Fig. 3a), ~4.1 kpc (STREAMFINDER mean); = 0.265 +- 0.008 mas (DR2, no contamination correction); omega Cen 5630 +- 100 pc (Braga+2018, arXiv:1802.03578).
  • Ibata, Malhan & Martin 2019 (arXiv:1901.07566): Fimbulthul anchor-point distance 4.22 +- 0.01 kpc (orbit fit). Extinction SFD98 + Schlafly & Finkbeiner 2011.
  • Ibata+2021 (arXiv:2012.05245): per-star dSF (DR2 detection run; the local streamfinder_ibata2021_edr3.fits is VizieR J/ApJ/914/123 table 1, "stars detected in Gaia DR2, with updated EDR3 astrometry"; Fimbulthul = Stream 16). Agent's reduction: dSF falls from ~5.5 kpc (l ~ -57) to ~3.0 kpc (l ~ -29); knee box (b 30-42, l -55..-40) median 4.1 kpc (16-84%: 3.6-4.7), median EDR3 plx 0.248 mas.
  • Ibata+2024 (arXiv:2311.17202; our catalogue): no distance column (G0, (BP-RP)0 dereddened); distances only as the Fig. 3 map; stream 55 "~3 kpc".
  • Simpson+2020 GALAH (arXiv:1911.01548): assumed (m-M)0 = 12.9 (3.8 kpc) for the Ibata sample vs 13.7 for omega Cen.
  • Kuzma+2021 (arXiv:2108.02531): 3 RR Lyrae within 5 deg: 5.2 +- 0.6 kpc. Kuzma+2026 (arXiv:2605.23474): omega Cen dynamical 5.29 +- 0.2 kpc; no tail distances.
  • Malhan+2022 (arXiv:2202.07660): weighted-mean parallax (Lindegren zero-point), no gradient.
  • Youakim+2023 (arXiv:2307.03035) quotes "Fimbulthul spans 2.4-7.2 kpc (Malhan+2022)": UNVERIFIED (not found in Malhan+2022). Full per-paper notes: the agent report (session); PDFs/text in the session scratchpad.

    • Implication for this project: the literature puts the knee at ~0.70-0.75 of omega Cen's distance; our CMD-shift track (stream54_cmd_distance.py, relative to members at b 15-20) gives 0.88-0.92 and is the outlier.

docs.title: CMD mask plan: Fable and Codex (2026-10-23)
docs.text:
User requirement: isochrone-based CMD masks broadened by photometric errors (vs magnitude) plus the cluster's intrinsic width from error deconvolution. Plan (Claude): MIST ridge; per-star errors from WSDB flux_over_error; per-bin deconvolution with a field term; mask |r| < k sqrt(s_int^2 + e^2).

Fable (checks on the cached cluster sample): MIST + 0.085 matches the MS but the cluster RGB is +0.045..0.055 redder and the SGB

= 0.2 mag fainter -> correct the ridge on the cluster; the G0 ~19.6 "limit" is the raw G < 20 cut (A_G 0.31), so the faint MS must be extrapolated; intrinsic width evaluated at the template-frame magnitude, photometric error at the star's own G; MS core Gaussian (no resolvable bMS/rMS bimodality in Gaia; dBIC <= 0), mildly red-skewed (binaries); RGB narrow core + red tail and 20-30 per cent field at the cluster PM -> empirical band; no crowding gradient at 20-40'; HB excluded; k: S/sqrt(B) flat for k 1.4-2 for a Gaussian on a flat background; default k = 2 and check S/N(k) on phi1 18-22. Against: the empirical density mask already encodes most of this; the Neyman-Pearson optimum is a likelihood ratio P_stream/P_field.

Codex: fit unsmoothed measurements (the old template's smoothing adds ~0.06 mag in colour); sigma = 1.0857/flux_over_error, band errors in quadrature; regularised mixture / extreme deconvolution with a contaminant term (single Gaussian as baseline); separate segments or 2-D around the TO/SGB; reddening uncertainty correlated along (1.339, 2.740); population gradients make the annulus mixture an assumption for the stream; evaluate intrinsic width at the cluster-equivalent magnitude; faint BP can be biased; choose k by injections / completeness per magnitude and phase; existing-code issues: "95 per cent" mask is not 95 per cent completeness, dm fit compares on a dm-dependent domain, dereddened cache lacks an ID-alignment check (now asserted), dm-relation metadata vs execution mismatch.

Implemented (bin/streams/gaia_cmd_mask.py): segments MS (colour residual, MIST + quadratic offset), RGB (colour residual, MIST + constant offset; RGB branch = steep post-SGB part of the isochrone), TO/SGB (empirical cluster ridge in colour bins joined to the MS and RGB ridges; ellipse distance; colour width = MS intrinsic at 17.7, magnitude width calibrated to 95.4 per cent control- subtracted completeness); per-star errors (cluster) / sky-median sigma(G) (stream stars without fetched errors); sigma_dm = 0.1.

docs.title: codex T1T2 next steps 2026 10 10
docs.text: The premise needs one correction: the frame swap changes \(z_\odot\) as well as \(V_{\odot,y}\) and \(R_0\): 0 to 17 pc, 252.24 to 232.24 km/s, and 8.178 to 8.122 kpc (frames.py:16–18).
