Fit a nested Hunter comparison with amplitude \(A=0\) versus \(A>0\). Jointly optimize cluster distance and both PMs, halo flattening, disc normalization, and host normalization under identical external constraints, release assumptions, sample, bandwidths, and numerical budgets. Start both fits from multiple locations and inspect boundaries. The existing 4D grid fixes PMs, and the broader size sweep fixes distance, amplitude, and catalogue PMs; neither substitutes for this comparison. bin/streams/grid4.py:20, bin/streams/bar3d_sweep.py:29, bin/streams/bar3d_sweep.py:41

There is an implementation trap: the direct hunter24_axi branch returns before applying axi_variant or mass_scale. Use the common amplitude-zero construction, or explicitly verify that the null actually changes when its host parameters change. Add an amplitude-zero force-equivalence test. src/ocen_dm/streams/restricted.py:80, src/ocen_dm/streams/restricted.py:99, src/ocen_dm/streams/restricted.py:110

Then require:

  1. Stable score differences and sky-conditioned residuals across paired seeds and increasing resolution.
  2. Axisymmetric-truth mocks processed through both complete fits, measuring false bar preference.
  3. Barred-truth mocks measuring power and interval coverage, including contaminants and plausible release-model departures.
  4. Prediction of withheld contiguous stream segments, with the split declared before fitting.

Even successful tests would reject the specified axisymmetric family under stated assumptions, not prove impossibility for every unbarred potential.

Bar constraints, angle tension, and remaining misfit

Report current parameter values as preferred sampled solutions, without confidence errors. Use paired seeds during comparisons, then independent seeds to validate selected candidates. Demonstrate stability of differences, not merely equal release counts: changing resolution also changes release-time spacing and which chi bins pass the particle threshold. bin/streams/grid4_common.py:55, src/ocen_dm/streams/score.py:252, bin/streams/seed_test.py:11

The block bootstrap is a sensitivity diagnostic. It resamples unequal-population spatial blocks and computes its score contrast between two models selected on the original data. Its variance inflation is not a universal \(N_{\rm eff}\), and its sign frequency is not a calibrated model-selection probability. Do not turn it into a likelihood temperature or combine it with seed scatter without a crossed calibration experiment. bin/streams/bootstrap_grid4.py:17, bin/streams/bootstrap_grid4.py:30

Present the low-angle preference alongside nuisance pulls and residuals. The recorded 28-degree candidate uses \(d=5.801\) kpc; the 16-degree candidate also shifts to \(5.616\) kpc, about 3.7 adopted distance errors above 5.43 kpc. Thus the external tension is not confined to the literature-angle solution. Neither candidate is a converged optimum. results/plot_data/bar_profile_refinement_20261013/fit_an28.json:540, results/plot_data/bar_profile_refinement_20261013/fit_an16.json:387, docs/STREAM_PM_REFINEMENT_2026-10-13.md:21, docs/STREAM_PM_REFINEMENT_2026-10-13.md:107

Show unpenalized scores, external-measurement penalties, and prior-conditioned results separately. The older free-angle fitter uses a 0.15-kpc distance prior and an optional angle prior, whereas the later refinement defaults to 0.05 kpc. Those are different inference setups. bin/streams/fit_bar_ocen.py:28, bin/streams/fit_bar_ocen.py:35, bin/streams/refine_bar_profiles.py:169

Do not claim that slowdown, another bar, or another escape law is excluded: several comparisons freeze nuisance parameters, and the escape-law note explicitly limits its conclusion to that pilot. Likewise, the RV encounter statistic is a diagnostic, not an ancestry probability. bin/streams/phase2_variants.py:20, docs/STREAM_PM_REFINEMENT_2026-10-13.md:211, bin/streams/backtrack_barred_release.py:4

Correctness and reproducibility blockers

  • The background uses constant density everywhere without implementing finite support. Specify a proper normalized background and treatment of selection before interpreting likelihood ratios inferentially. src/ocen_dm/streams/score.py:249, src/ocen_dm/streams/score.py:278
  • The documented fit_bar_ocen.py --conditional invocation is rejected by its parser: the flag is inspected in sys.argv but never registered before parse_args(). bin/streams/fit_bar_ocen.py:34, bin/streams/fit_bar_ocen.py:40
  • Cache existence is sometimes treated as configuration identity. For example, grid2’s filename omits release count and release window despite exposing both as arguments. Require validated configuration/source/input fingerprints before reusing publication results; this is a contamination risk, not evidence that contamination occurred. bin/streams/spray_bar_grid2.py:35, bin/streams/spray_bar_grid2.py:45
  • The inspected conditional-score tests exercise no measured RVs or nonzero PM correlations. Add analytic correlated-covariance, RV marginalization, background-normalization, invalid-input, and CLI regression tests. tests/test_score_conditional.py:9, tests/test_score_conditional.py:24

I recommend six figures, with validation details and chi ordering in an appendix.

Figure Required content 1 Data: sky and PMs; RV locations; alternative-selection ridge with its limits clearly marked. 2 Central comparison: fairly refitted axisymmetric, literature-angle barred, and freely fitted barred models against the same data. 3 Residuals: sky-conditioned PM predictions, sky residuals, RVs, and regional contributions; include model spread and numerical variation. 4 Profile maps: angle–size–speed degeneracy, boundaries, external pulls, and raw versus penalized scores. 5 Calibration: axisymmetric-null recovery, barred recovery, and paired-seed/resolution stability. 6 Selected robustness results: physical residual changes plus score changes, distinguishing frozen pilots from refitted comparisons.

Use common plotting scales and enclosed-probability bands. Existing profile plots normalize every column to its peak, which can visually promote sparse branches; the conditional plotting script also omits measurement-error convolution. State that distinction in captions or plot observation-convolved predictions. bin/streams/plot_profile_stage1.py:41, bin/streams/plot_conditional_model.py:6

Use the MNRAS sequence Introduction → Data → Methods → Model comparison → Conditional bar constraints → Discussion → Conclusions. Put residual misfit beside the principal comparison, rather than postponing it to a robustness section.

  1. Verified versus assumed. I read the cited implementation, tests, notes, and selected saved results; I checked saved sweep maxima and refinement candidates. I did not reproduce integrations, validate raw catalogue membership, or independently verify literature values and novelty claims. The attempted score-test execution stopped because the available Python lacks NumPy; no tests passed in this review. Nothing was modified.

  2. Strongest argument against my answer. I may be demanding too much calibration for a paper whose main contribution is a qualitative dynamical explanation. The documented axisymmetric failures span several model choices, so a focused comparison paper could be justified before precise inference is ready. That supports a narrower paper; it still does not support “impossible” or calibrated bar measurements. docs/STREAM_KNEE_INVESTIGATION.md:9

  3. What I would need to check to be sure. The matched null/bar fits and mock calibration above; replay of publication results from frozen inputs; membership-excluded control-field detection; tracer validation at the final fitted states; and physical admissibility of the scaled host, including density positivity and bar-force strength. The amplitude parameter multiplies a full-minus-axisymmetric potential term, so it should not be interpreted directly as bar mass. src/ocen_dm/streams/restricted.py:95, src/ocen_dm/streams/restricted.py:106

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
The code supports the central failure mode in the packet. The grid selects trailing particles with \(b>15\) and \(-75<l<-20\), then estimates a track in 2-degree \(b\) bins. The score drops model bins flagged as unreliable and sums chi-square only over the remaining bins; it does not penalise the masked bins. Thus a fold that makes a bin’s mixture fit unreliable can remove that bin’s contribution to the score. spray_bar_grid.py:21-29, spray_bar_grid.py:43-48, track.py:15-16, track.py:47-63

There is one boundary to that claim: the track bins end at \(b=43\), and particles outside the longitude cut are discarded before fitting. Debris beyond those cuts cannot affect the current score through those bins. track.py:15, spray_bar_grid.py:44-45

docs.title: Recommended design
docs.text:
(a) Extracting the model track. I would not order particles by release age or progenitor-orbit arc length and treat that ordering as the stream coordinate. The code gives each particle a release age, but does not show that age is monotonic along the present-day stream; the progenitor orbit is also distinct from the paths of the released particles. spray.py:58-63, spray.py:70-83

For this comparison, use a local model distribution conditioned on sky position, not a single globally ordered curve:

model_conditionals(particles, sky_bandwidth, observable_bandwidths) -> LocalModel

At each observed star or track location \(s=(l,b)\), use nearby model particles to estimate the conditional mean and covariance of \(q=(\mathrm{pmra},\mathrm{pmdec},v_{\rm los},\log d)\). This can retain distinct kinematic branches where a fold overlaps the observed sky region. Keep release age attached as a diagnostic or for a separately justified young-debris cut; do not use it to force a branch assignment. A principal curve or nearest-neighbour chain could still be useful for plots, but branch crossings and particle noise make either a risky basis for the likelihood.

(b) Data-model comparison and overshoot. Prefer per-star comparisons in a local sky window over matching one summary point per \(b\) bin. The existing data product includes per-star \(v_{\rm los}\) values and errors for the selected stars, while the current track estimator fits only \(l\), pmra, and pmdec by \(b\) bin. measure_track.py:25-30, measure_track.py:36-39, track.py:41-45

A concrete initial objective is a local conditional likelihood with a broad background component:

score_stars(data_stars, local_model, selection, weights) -> Score
\[ \log L_{\rm data} = \sum_i \log\left[ \sum_{j\in \mathcal N(s_i)} w_j\,K_h(s_i-s_j)\, \mathcal N(q_i\mid q_j,\ C_i+H) + \epsilon\,p_{\rm bg}(q_i) \right], \]

where \(C_i\) contains the star’s measurement covariance and \(H\) is a predeclared intrinsic smoothing covariance. Normalize or scale coordinates before choosing bandwidths; the observables have different units. Do not treat every spray particle as a measured star: spray density and release sampling are not established here as a survey selection model. The current grid score also uses only three observables, so adding \(v_{\rm los}\) and distance requires explicit error and covariance handling, not just extra terms. spray_bar_grid.py:21-29, frames.py:48-56

I would keep “debris where the data have none” as a separate, initially diagnostic penalty, not silently fold it into the per-star likelihood. For example,

\[ P_{\rm out} = \frac{\sum_j w_j\,\mathbf 1[\mathrm{age}_j<600]\, \mathbf 1[d(s_j,\mathrm{tube})>r]} {\sum_j w_j\,\mathbf 1[\mathrm{age}_j<600]}. \]

A term \(\lambda P_{\rm out}\) is easy to compute, but it is not a calibrated likelihood without a defined observed footprint, member-selection function, and a defensible \(\lambda\). The data script applies a stream-membership and sky cut; it does not establish completeness or a detection probability outside that selected sample. measure_track.py:19-29

(c) Smoothness and compute. Keep the same release draws across candidate models, increase particle count until rankings stabilise, and use kernel estimates rather than hard bins and fit-success masks. The grid already passes seed=1 for each model, and spray uses that seed for release times and offsets; that is a useful common-random-number starting point. spray_bar_grid.py:40-45, spray.py:64-75 The current mask thresholds and finite-bin mixture fits introduce discrete changes in which bins contribute. spray_bar_grid.py:26-29, track.py:33-38

The grid filters to the trailing arm only after calling spray; the spray creates paired leading and trailing particles. So “release only trailing” could save compute, but it would require changing the release/integration path, not merely moving the existing filter. spray.py:42-55, spray.py:74-83, spray_bar_grid.py:43-45

(d) Cheapest validation. First freeze a visual ranking of the existing 45 grid models using the same plot limits and blinded parameter labels, then compare it with the new score’s ranking and inspect disagreements. But the grid JSON written by this script stores binned tracks and counts, not particle phase space, so it cannot evaluate the proposed fold-aware objective by itself. spray_bar_grid.py:47-48 The cheapest meaningful check is to regenerate the 45 candidates with fixed shared random draws at a moderate particle count, compute the new score, then rerun only the best, worst, and most discordant cases at higher counts. Treat rank stability across those counts as a required check before using the objective for optimization.

Concrete signatures:

extract_local_model(particles, sky_bandwidth, observable_bandwidths) -> LocalModel
score_stars(data_stars, local_model, selection_model=None) -> Score
overshoot_fraction(particles, observed_tube, age_max_myr, tube_radius) -> float
score_model(data_stars, particles, local_model, overshoot_weight=None) -> Score

docs.title: Verified in code vs assumed
docs.text:
Verified: the spray returns arm labels and release ages; the grid selects trailing particles, applies the stated sky cuts, fits by \(b\) bins, and omits masked bins from chi-square; the observed-data script saves per-star \(v_{\rm los}\) values and errors. spray.py:58-63, spray.py:81-84, spray_bar_grid.py:21-29, spray_bar_grid.py:43-48, measure_track.py:36-39

Assumed from the packet, not verified by reading these files: the visual fold’s location and age, the 10–40 particle counts in knee bins, the small data-error values, and the claim that the best current grid models visibly overshoot. I did not inspect model plots or rerun the grid.

docs.title: Strongest argument against this design
docs.text: The local conditional likelihood can reward a model for placing some particles near every observed star while ignoring how much debris it predicts elsewhere. The overshoot term is meant to address that, but without a selection function its weight and tube definition are subjective. A single curve matched to binned data is easier to explain and may be more stable at low particle counts; if the folds are well separated in sky position and the scientific target is only the main arm, the additional distribution model may be unnecessary complexity.

docs.title: What I would check to be sure
docs.text:
• Inspect particle-level outputs and plots for representative good, bad, and borderline grid models; confirm the reported fold and quantify branch occupancy.
  • Establish what the stream-member catalogue selection permits us to call “no members,” especially beyond the observed track end.
  • Test whether the local likelihood’s rankings persist as particle count and smoothing bandwidth change.
  • Check whether the 29 \(v_{\rm los}\) stars overlap the spatial range used for the track fit and whether their errors support a useful constraint.
  • Compare new-objective rankings with independent visual ratings, and inspect every disagreement before trusting a best-fit model.

docs.title: Codex review: pragmatic plan for the 9-D emulator training set (2026-10-17)
docs.text:
Codex CLI, effort medium, read-only. Adopted: calibration tranche first, float64 sprays + per-star numerator/denominator, combined-corner preflight, corotation root per variant host, transitive source + input-file hashes. Not adopted: per-bin per-star contributions (recomputable from the stored sprays).

The noise premise does not match the proposed target: the existing study explicitly scores pooled debris; its scatter does not establish fixed-bin noise or bias (neff_study.py:44). Equal chi weights also retain density dependence through the foreground/background denominator (score.py:327).

Changes ranked by importance:

  1. Launch a calibration tranche, then gate the remaining jobs. Keep 256k provisionally; compare 128k/256k at equal cost using the actual fixed-bin score. Give a few representative points 8–16 independent seeds, including sparse/extreme cases, rather than treating four seeds at eight points as validated noise calibration. Save per-star numerator and denominator in float64; estimate total-score noise across seeds, preserving cross-star covariance. n_eff measures joint foreground concentration only (score.py:325). The existing convergence test concerns pooled scoring and only two sample sizes (test_score_conditional.py:113). Neither resolution is established as sufficient.

  2. Preflight the combined physical extremes. vc_target and halo_q compose algebraically, with rejection of nonpositive halo normalization (mw_variants.py:38); the target-speed test exercises only default flattening (test_mw_variants.py:27). Check combined corners for achieved speed, finite forces and nonnegative total density. Especially check large amplitude/size: the host adds a scaled difference of baryonic potentials, without a density-positivity check (restricted.py:94). Corotation alone does not establish physical admissibility.

  3. Keep the S mapping, but implement corotation independently of the old helper. Solve \(v_c(R)/R=\Omega_b\) using each point’s variant host; require a bracketed root and upper limit ≥0.8. The existing helper uses the original host and interpolation, so cannot implement your proposed constraint (refine_bar_profiles.py:57). Your mapping samples S uniformly conditional on the other parameters; it does not sample uniformly over the constrained physical volume. That is acceptable for emulator design; specify inference priors separately.

  4. Strengthen preservation before launch. Save every returned particle, including negative/out-of-range chi, plus release index and age_cut_myr. Preserve chi/age in float64: hard bin/age cuts make float32 rounding potentially consequential (score.py:282, score.py:292). Add per-bin counts and joint/u contributions; current diagnostics expose only their aggregate (score.py:330). Tracks can wait. xv is optional for present-coordinate rescoring; the proposed observables already supply the wrapper’s inputs (grid4_common.py:90).

  5. Separate spray identity from score identity. A scoring change should create new score records without invalidating valid sprays. Hash external potential files, mass profile, frame/projection inputs, ordered data and transitive source dependencies—not merely the five named sources. Those inputs enter through external files and imported transformations (restricted.py:97, grid4_common.py:17, frames.py:21). Use unique temporary files per worker and verify artifact hashes before skipping.

Safe later: GP/kernel choice, final chi cutoff, correction implementation and additional design points—provided the particles and calibration quantities above survive. Correction validation must precede interpreting emulator likelihood differences. Fixed-bin densities themselves divide by random bin occupancy, so the proposed delta correction is not automatically complete (score.py:323).

1. Verified versus assumed. Verified the cited scoring, generation, host construction and tests by reading; no tests or simulations run. I assume the quoted timings and memory measurements are representative. Changing vc_target leaves the solar frame fixed; I assume that is intentional (frames.py:22).

2. Strongest argument against this answer. More independent 128k points could improve nine-dimensional coverage more than deeper calibration, especially for exploratory emulation. The existing evidence does not resolve that tradeoff for fixed bins.

3. Needed for confidence. Fixed-bin replicated resolution comparisons; combined-host density/force checks; float32 replay comparisons; chi integration convergence beyond the default 240 trajectory samples (spray.py:103, spray.py:163); interrupted-write/resume tests; and independent simulator validation near emulator-supported modes.

docs.title: Codex review: bias and noise of the conditional KDE stream likelihood (2026-10-17)
docs.text:
Question: see JOURNAL 2026-10-17 (n_eff study). Codex CLI, effort high, read-only.

Use replicated randomized integration first, a corrected delta method second, and a surrogate only after those pass calibration. Do not trust proposal (a) as written.

The proposed \(+\tfrac12\operatorname{Var}(\log L_i)\) is generally not the bias correction for the implemented likelihood ratio. Also, its particle-variance formula assumes an i.i.d. sample that this release design does not provide: epochs are deterministic, offsets are random, and particles are subsequently selected by trajectory-dependent \(\chi>0\). grid4_common.py:55–57, spray.py:58–61, score.py:282–286.

My priority order is (b), corrected (a), (c), (e), (d).

(a): correct the estimator before estimating its uncertainty.

For unbiased estimators \(\widehat A_i,\widehat B_i\) of the mixture numerator and denominator, write [ \widehat\ell_i=\log\widehat A_i-\log\widehat B_i. ] The second-order correction is [ \widehat\ell_{i,\mathrm{bc}} =\widehat\ell_i+ \frac12\left[ \frac{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\widehat A_i)}{\widehat A_i^2} -\frac{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\widehat B_i)}{\widehat B_i^2} \right]. ] In contrast, [ \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\ell_i)\approx \frac{V_{A_i}}{A_i^2}+\frac{V_{B_i}}{B_i^2} -\frac{2C_{A_iB_i}}{A_iB_i}. ] Covariance belongs in the noise estimate; it cancels from this leading log-ratio bias correction. These expressions differ for the ratio actually calculated. score.py:327–329.

There is another complication: both densities divide by the random number of accepted particles. Simply treating their sample means as unbiased skips this selection-normalization bias. score.py:282–286, score.py:313–324.

A cleaner calculation preserves contributions from every eligible release epoch, including rejected ones. Let \(I_j\) indicate acceptance, \(G_{ij}\) be its joint kernel and \(H_{ij}\) its along-stream kernel. Define [ X_{ij}=I_j[(1-\epsilon)G_{ij}+\epsilon g_ug_{w,i}],\qquad Y_{ij}=I_j[(1-\epsilon)H_{ij}+\epsilon g_u]. ] Then \(\sum_jX_{ij}/\sum_jY_{ij}\) equals the existing pooled likelihood whenever its foreground bin exists. Apply bias and covariance calculations to these raw sums. This retains the fluctuating acceptance normalization explicitly.

For deterministic epochs, variation across particles includes variation in their epoch-dependent expectations. Consequently, ordinary sample variance divided by particle count need not estimate seed variance. Particle leave-one-out jackknifing inherits that problem. Contiguous split halves also change the release-age distribution.

I would start with 8–16 independent complete replicates, retaining raw sums, and estimate the correction from replicate covariance. Use a matched, interleaved delete-group jackknife only as a cheaper candidate to validate against those replicates. A split estimator [ 2\ell_{\mathrm{full}}-\tfrac12(\ell_{\mathrm{half1}}+\ell_{\mathrm{half2}}) ] can cancel leading \(1/N\) bias under the appropriate sampling design; it does not guarantee cancellation in sparse tails.

At \(n_{\rm eff}=3\)–10, neither delta correction nor jackknifing deserves an accuracy claim without replication. Effective count alone does not characterize skewness, denominator variation or background transitions. The implemented diagnostic measures only foreground joint-kernel concentration. score.py:325–334.

For total noise, preserve cross-star covariance: [ \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\ell)\approx \operatorname{Var}!\left[ \sum_i\left(\frac{\delta A_i}{A_i}-\frac{\delta B_i}{B_i}\right) \right]. ] Summing per-star variances is insufficient. Estimate this total directly across replicates, including variability introduced by the correction itself.

(b): highest priority, but benchmark equal computational cost.

Use scrambled Sobol points over release time plus the four Gaussian escape variables, with independent scrambles for error estimation. Alternatively, retain the deterministic time grid and first test stratified offsets. The four underlying normal draws are explicit in the release code. spray.py:58–61.

Use power-of-two Sobol nets and estimate variance between independent scrambles, not between their dependent points. Randomized integration can give unbiased raw integral estimates; applying a logarithm or ratio still introduces bias. SciPy’s Sobol documentation.

Antithetic Gaussian deviations about their prescribed means are worth testing; opposite launch arms are not substitutes for antithetic samples of the trailing-arm distribution. The release code assigns those arms different signed offsets. spray.py:55–65.

Use common random numbers for local comparisons. Measure their actual reduction in difference variance; they do not reduce marginal bias. Preserve random-variable identities when changing particle count—the current successive array-sized draws do not supply a nested realization of every offset component. spray.py:58–61.

(c): useful after identifying influential release regions; “every member above 30” is the wrong objective.

For proposal \(q(t)\) and target release law \(p(t)\), [ \widehat f_i=N^{-1}\sum_j[p(t_j)/q(t_j)]G_{ij} ] is unbiased for the corresponding unnormalized integral. Self-normalization, selection conditioning, ratios and logarithms reintroduce bias. Carry weights through the raw \(X,Y\) sums above.

Parameter-dependent proposals are valid if their densities and weights are correct. They need not be parameter-independent. For operational simplicity, learn a frozen mixture from a broad pilot design, including a substantial uniform component—say 20%—to preserve support.

Allocate effort using contribution to total-score variance per unit cost, rather than minimum Kish count. Some members should remain background-dominated; forcing their foreground effective counts upward can waste most of the computation. The existing mixture explicitly permits that regime. score.py:327–329.

(d): hold bandwidth fixed during numerical convergence tests.

Define the target as the infinite-particle likelihood at a specified bandwidth. Otherwise numerical convergence and changes to the statistical model become inseparable.

Measurement-error convolution is principled, but it does not determine additional smoothing in release time or sky position. The implementation already adds Gaia covariance and radial-velocity error variance to its kernel widths; setting those widths directly equal to measurement errors would add another smoothing contribution. score.py:308–321.

Choose additional widths through predictive checks and physical-model assumptions, then report bandwidth sensitivity. Do not enlarge them solely to obtain affordable numerical noise.

(e): appropriate for exploration, with two restrictions.

First, a GP nugget cannot absorb systematic estimator bias. Train on corrected scores only after validating that correction across the design domain.

Second, common random numbers create correlated simulation errors across design points. A diagonal heteroscedastic nugget then misrepresents their covariance. Either retain replicate identities and estimate that covariance, or use independent training randomizations and reserve common random numbers for local contrasts.

For tempering, [ \ell_\beta=\beta\ell,\quad b_\beta=\beta b,\quad V_\beta=\beta^2V. ] For segment powers, use \(\beta^\mathsf T\Sigma\beta\), retaining cross-segment covariance. Calibrate powers against observational/model misspecification and recovery coverage, separately from simulation noise. Holmes–Walker provides an information-matching rationale, not an automatic remedy for correlated members or simulation error. Holmes & Walker.

Require direct replicated evaluations near posterior modes and between competing modes. A raw bias tolerance of 10 may suffice for exploration; at \(\beta=1\), a parameter-dependent error of 10 can distort posterior odds by \(e^{10}\).

There is no simple reformulation that makes the current target unbiased.

Unbiased joint-density estimates do not make their ratio unbiased. Even unbiased \(L_i\) estimates would not generally give an unbiased product when they share spray particles. Exponentiating an unbiased log-score is also biased.

Exact pseudo-marginal inference requires a nonnegative unbiased estimate of the whole likelihood. Correlated pseudo-marginal methods can tolerate large marginal log noise when the proposal-ratio noise is controlled, so “sd must equal one” is too categorical; the present estimator nevertheless fails the unbiased-likelihood prerequisite. Deligiannidis, Doucet & Pitt.

Russian-roulette/Poisson constructions require separate proofs of unbiasedness, sign, finite variance and cost. They are a research project here. Signed-estimator complications are documented by Lyne et al.. Synthetic likelihood or ABC changes the inferential target and may discard useful distributional information. An analytically evaluable conditional mixture could remove repeated KDE integration, but introduces approximation error requiring its own validation.

1. Verified versus assumed

Verified by reading the four requested files fully and inspecting relevant tests:

  • The study explicitly uses pooled scoring. The wrapper itself does not default to pooled scoring; a new exploration must request it explicitly. neff_study.py:43–44, grid4_common.py:80–86, score.py:233.
  • Recalculation from the stored 40 runs reproduces the reported score means. At 256k, individual score SDs are 41.5 for A and 22.9 for B; 56.3 describes their paired difference. The difference’s standard errors across the four resolutions are 42.4, 35.0, 25.2, 17.6, rather than approximately 20 throughout. neff_study_20261017.json:1.
  • The convergence test checks one pair of realizations at two sizes; the effective-count test checks identical contributors and score invariance. Neither establishes a bias bound or calibrated noise estimate. test_score_conditional.py:113–137.
  • Resumption identifies completed runs only by model label, size and seed, then saves current model parameters alongside retained runs. Changed models or scoring code can silently mix incompatible results. Add configuration/data/code fingerprints before expanding the campaign. neff_study.py:51–60.

I assume the intended target is the continuous-release, infinite-particle, fixed-bandwidth conditional score; that the catalogue’s member selection permits this conditional likelihood; and that simulator draws are computational integration variables rather than a physical finite population. Those assumptions need scientific validation.

I could not execute the tests: the available Python lacks NumPy and pytest. Nothing was modified.

2. Strongest argument against my recommendation

Randomized integration may deliver little benefit where trajectory dynamics and the hard \(\chi>0\) selection produce sharp boundaries. Those boundaries are present in this calculation. spray.py:156–163, score.py:282.

Splitting a fixed budget among replicates also leaves each replicate sparser. Higher-order bias and correction noise could outweigh the benefit. A larger conventional spray with targeted importance sampling might therefore be cheaper and more reliable. Decide using measured wall-time efficiency, not the nominal convergence rate.

3. Checks needed before trusting it

These are proposed acceptance criteria:

  1. Analytic fixtures: Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture streams with known convolved densities; include correlated PM errors, missing/measured velocities, background transitions and random acceptance. Across repeated samples, require [ |\widehat b|+1.96\,\mathrm{SE}(\widehat b)<10 ] for total corrected score, with reference uncertainty included.

  2. Real-model references: audit at least 20 points spanning both candidate modes, sparse regions and parameter extremes. Build independently randomized, substantially higher-resolution references. Require reference SE below 2, a 95% bound on further-resolution drift below 3, and the same bias criterion above. Increase repetitions until the bound is resolved; five seeds are insufficient.

  3. Noise calibration: use approximately 200 independent evaluations at selected audit points. Require empirical variance divided by mean predicted variance in 0.8–1.25, standardized residual mean within 0.2 of zero, and nominal 95% interval coverage in 92–98%. Check total scores, segment scores and paired parameter differences separately.

  4. Equal-cost comparisons: compare conventional sampling, stratification, scrambled Sobol, antithetics and importance sampling using wall time and MSE against the reference, including correction noise. Promote a method only if its MSE reduction is statistically resolved.

  5. Posterior validation: on independent simulator evaluations near posterior support, require weighted log-score contrast errors below 0.5, including uncertainty. Test posterior coverage on mocks with realistic selection and model discrepancy; 90% intervals should cover in approximately 86–94% of at least 200 recovery experiments. A finite audit supports accuracy over the tested domain, not a uniform guarantee over all nine dimensions.

docs.title: dm(phi1) refit by iteration: Fable and Codex (2026-10-23)
docs.text: Briefing (Claude): masks from stream_masks.py (CMD-filtered, cross-selected PM/sky fits); dm from MS colour centring in 3 bins (-0.32/-0.53/-0.75 at phi1 16/20/24) with the old hand-marked windows; proposed plan: refit dm with converged masks, 2-D CMD likelihood on a fixed observed-G domain, more bins, iterate dm <-> masks to convergence, injection and null tests.

docs.title: Codex (read code + JSON; no runs)
docs.text:
• Iteration is circular in principle: PM/sky masks are trained on cmd_pass, which depends on dm; dropping the CMD cut from the dm selection does not break that. Numerical convergence does not establish unbiased dm.
  • Current dm estimator: colour window and template-G limit move with trial dm; first zero crossing returned; bootstrap keeps the red-control normalisation fixed and drops failed roots (nanstd).
  • Bug (confirmed): displayed PM background integrated over +-3 deg while the on-window uses SKYH(u) (2.0-2.7 at phi1 13-23). Display only.
  • Not converged (confirmed): pmra track at phi1 9 moved 0.32 mas/yr in the last of 6 iterations; no non-convergence flag.
  • dm off-sky control (4-12 deg) does not exclude the upper branch.
  • fit_pm: truncated data, untruncated Gaussian; width floored after fit; 1-parameter errors; sky significance excess/sqrt(B). Thresholds are heuristic scores.
  • "95%" borders are conditional on the other masks, not population widths.
  • Reproducibility: CMD-pass cache keyed on JSON mtime; parameter JSON overwritten before the dm step.
  • Recommended: freeze the analysis; normalised on/off CMD mixture in (c0, G0) on a fixed domain; MS + TO/SGB jointly with separate diagnostics; non-overlapping bins, keep weak bins; dm near the cluster unconstrained (cap = assumption; spray prior compromises independence); conservative faint-BP limit, compare G-RP; joint model later. Counter-argument: freezing/holding out loses signal; end-to-end injections should decide.

docs.title: Fable (quick checks on cached data, scratch scripts)
docs.text:
• dm is insensitive to the masks: old vs converged masks 14-18 -0.32 -> -0.29, 18-22 -0.53 -> -0.51, 22-26 -0.75 -> -0.79. Sky-centre jumps irrelevant (99% of on-sample unchanged). CMD-pass sample changes 1-5% for dm +-0.1. One extra pass suffices.
  • Background normalisation (red-control ratio) is the main systematic: PM-shifted nulls give CMD-pass excesses of -30% to +50% of B (e.g. +76 on 160 at 18-22, "6 sigma"). Detections at phi1 4-12 and 24-32 not secure; near-cluster excess (50-80% of B) probably real.
  • MS centring has no detection test: on nulls it returns dm -0.6..-1.4 +- 0.2-0.4; 26-30 (-1.14) is noise, 24-28 marginal.
  • Colour lever arm 1/(dc/dG) = 6-14: 0.01 mag colour systematic = 0.06-0.14 mag in dm. Faint split: G 19-19.6 gives more negative dm than G < 19 in all bins; restricting to the calibrated template range moves dm by +0.07..+0.11.
  • Injection bias of MS centring <= 0.09 (sky-shifted null), up to 0.17 (PM-shifted null). Hess-template / moving-domain methods biased.
  • Near cluster: dm at phi1 2-6 = +0.03 [-0.12, +0.10] (null gives -1.2), so dm ~ 0 there is measured; 6-14 unconstrained.
  • pmra at phi1 7-17 is the anchored hand track (bins 1-3.9 sigma, not accepted).
  • Recommended: 2-D unbinned CMD likelihood (CMDMask template + LF weight, per-star errors, sigma_dm), field = off-sky KDE with free amplitude, fixed observed domain (G < 19.6, 0.3 < c0 < 1.3, G0 > 16.3); full / MS-only / TO-SGB-only per bin; 4-deg bins step 2 at 10-28 + one bin 0-8; gate on amplitude >= 3 sigma and null < 2 sigma; systematics budget (reddening scale, R, template range, [Fe/H] -1.9/-1.5); one mask re-run + one dm refit; then the joint mixture. Counter-argument: TO/SGB-only gives +-0.1-0.2, so pragmatic path = MS centring + gate + nulls + calibrated range, then go straight to the joint mixture.

docs.title: Fable review: is the outer bar-force demand robust, and what next (2026-10-21)
docs.text: Claude re-ran bin/streams/diagnostics/orbit_force_check.py and lz_and_fourier.py (run with OCEN_ROOT=, PYTHONPATH=src); numbers reproduce.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Along omega Cen's orbit the fitted bar's non-axisymmetric force averages to ~0 (|mean| <= 0.003 |F_axi| over 300-700 Myr; rms 0.12-0.13 vs 0.07 published); today at the cluster 0.057 vs 0.020. So the fit is NOT using the bar as a proxy for a static (axisymmetric) change (disc, halo q, v_c, frame, distance, PMs): it buys a TORQUE HISTORY. 12.5-deg best: Lz -609 (300 Myr ago) -> -512 today vs -561 -> -512 published; apocentre walks 7.1 -> 6.2 kpc over 1 Gyr (published 7.3 -> 6.95). The stream (300-700 Myr debris) records that history.
  • Robust against the axisymmetric alternatives; NOT established that it is m=2 co-rotating with the bar (the Hunter bar was the only form offered). m=1 lopsided halo, tilted/triaxial halo, bar-induced halo wake not excluded; spiral (pre-screen) and LMC (~0.01 |F_axi|) too weak.
  • Plausibility: m=2 radial amplitude at R0 (z 0) 0.062 (fitted) vs 0.017 (published); Hercules/OLR models use 0.01-0.02 (Dehnen 2000, 2000AJ....119..800D; Hunt & Bovy 2018, arXiv:1803.02358). A long bar x2 mass x1.3 length has ~3.4x the published far-field quadrupole; dynamical bar lengths are if anything shorter (Lucey+2023 arXiv:2206.01798; Vislosky+2024 2024MNRAS.528.3576V) than Wegg+2015's 5.0 kpc. Nothing known supplies ~2x the published quadrupole at 5-7 kpc.

docs.title: Recommendation (b): one discriminating batch at fixed 12.5-deg parameters (32k, CRN, ~14 sprays, ~20 min on 2 cores + ~1 h code)
docs.text: Host = published bar (A=S=1) + 'excess' (fitted minus published bar term) as a separate component with its own pattern speed and phase: control (Omega_2 = Omega_b, phase 0; must reproduce the fitted score within 100); Omega_2 = Omega_b at phase +45, +90; static (Omega_2 = 0) at 3 phases (triaxial-halo-like); Omega_2 = 22.5 (spiral-like) at 2 phases; Omega_2 = -33 (counter-rotating); optional static triaxial halo p = 0.85 at 2 PAs; published bar + disc_scale 0.8 / 1.2 at fixed v_c. Criteria relative to the 3808 gap (published -> fitted): any non-co-rotating configuration recovering > 70% -> generic outer non-axisymmetric force, pattern speed unidentified -> stop the bar-refit line, write it up as a constraint; only Omega_2 ~ Omega_b recovers (others < 30%) -> bar-locked -> long-bar refit with literature priors (2 angles, ~3 h on 8 cores) + Hercules tension; disc_scale recovering > 1000 -> add it to the design first. Against: fixed-parameter tests are unfair to alternatives (the published bar loses 3808 at fixed params); the honest alternative (d) is to stop now and report "the stream requires a non-axisymmetric force history ~2x the published bar's rms along the orbit".

docs.title: Fable review: why the 25-deg bar scatters its debris, and a targeted alternative-bar plan (2026-10-21)
docs.text: Read-only; diagnostics bin/streams/diagnostics/bar_diag.py, bar_diag2.py (Claude re-ran bar_diag2: force ratios, branch fractions and Jacobi energies reproduce).

docs.title: Mechanism (checked)
docs.text:
• Not chaos (shadow orbits e-fold > 300 Myr) and not a low-order resonance: omega Cen is retrograde (Lz -510), peri 1.5-2.2, apo 6.4-7.2 kpc, T_r 92 Myr; (Omega_b - Omega_phi)/Omega_r = 1.17 (25) / 1.13 (12.5); CR 6.29 / 6.79 kpc, OLR 10-11 kpc.
  • Branch = the less-bound (higher Jacobi energy) leading part of the debris released ~300-350 Myr ago: 25 deg E_J -105,160 vs track -107,130; it separates deterministically through later pericentre torques (Pearson+2017-type differential torquing).
  • The angles differ in the branch FRACTION (age 300-350, phi1 6-22: 60% vs 24%) and the released E_J width: the 25-deg model's 331-Myr release pericentre lies on the bar major axis (deepest of the last Gyr, r 1.54 kpc); the 12.5-deg one at -45 deg. Inferred (untested): bar-aligned release at the deepest pericentre widens E_J and feeds the branch -> set by angle, Omega_b and the INNER bar.

docs.title: Suspect bar parametrisation (checked)
docs.text:
• |F_nonaxi|max/|F_axi| at R 1.5-7 kpc (z 0): published Hunter24/Portail17 (A = S = 1) 0.23-0.29 / 0.19 / 0.13 / 0.08 / 0.04 (R <= 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7); best 25 deg (A 1.38, S 1.24) 0.29-0.40 / 0.34 / 0.25 / 0.19 / 0.135; best 12.5 (A 1.37, S 1.33) 0.27-0.37 / 0.36 / 0.27 / 0.21 / 0.16 -> 1.2-1.4x the published m>0 force inside 3 kpc but 2.3-3.5x at 5-7 kpc (omega Cen's apocentre). Quadrupole moment ~ A S^3 = 2.6 / 3.2 x published. S 1.14-1.33 puts the bar end at 5.7-6.6 kpc vs Wegg+2015 half-length 5.0 +- 0.2 kpc (arXiv:1504.01401).
  • The fits buy extra non-axisymmetric force at R > 4 kpc with bar parameters: first suspect for the common misfits (knee pmdec, Delta phi2 offsets, d at the band top, vc 223-225). The inflated OUTER bar is not what makes the branch.
  • Available: Hunter24 spiral (2 arms, Omega_sp 22.5, amplitude ~ (R/8.18)^2), implemented in src/ocen_dm/streams/spiral.py (pilot 2026-10-13 at frozen 28-deg params: +277/+317). Portail17 m>0 force within 2-8% of Hunter's (interchangeable).

docs.title: Plan (targeted)
docs.text: M-A "published bar + spiral arms": A = S = 1 fixed; angle, Omega_b free; spiral amplitude a_sp in [0, 1.5] and phase free (pattern speed 22.5). M-B null: A = S = 1, no spiral. Pre-screen (<= 1.5 h, 1-2 cores): (a) can the spiral supply ~0.1 of F_axi at 5-7 kpc; (b) four 32k sprays at the 12.5/25 best params with A=S=1, a_sp=1, phase 0/90; (c) cluster orbit in the spiral host. Then profile_nm --design step3 at 12.5, 20, 27.5 deg (2 chains x 40 at 128k, 4 x 256k): ~4.5 h; M-B at 2 angles ~2 h. Criteria: angle gap 12.5 vs 27.5 (< 300 -> angle not determined; > 1000 -> robust); knee pmdec residual < 0.3 mas/yr; Delta phi2 offsets halve; far-end density within 2x; branch R_pred at 25-27.5 <= 0.2 (Gaia-compatible) or ~0.5 (intrinsic); d and vc leave the edges; M-A better than M-B by > 500. Against: the branch mechanism (inner bar, release pericentre phase) is untouched by M-A; spiral phase/pattern speed degenerate with (Omega_b, angle); pilot gain small vs the 1885 gap. Cheaper complementary check: one 32k spray at the 25-deg best with Omega_b +-1.5 (release pericentre off the major axis) -> does the branch fraction respond?

docs.title: Fable: bar slowdown and the omega Cen stream -- importance, rewinding lessons, strategy (2026-10-23)
docs.text: Read-only review. Claude checked the arithmetic (phase lag c tau^2 with c = eta Omega^2 / 2: 12 / 25 / 48 deg at 350 / 500 / 700 Myr for eta 0.003, Omega 33.1; A S^3 of the slowing bar 700 Myr ago 0.80; alias time pi / 12 t.u. = 256 Myr). The orbit/phase numbers come from Fable's scratchpad AGAMA check (not in the repo).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• eta ~ 0.003 (Mannu+2026 4.5 km/s/kpc/Gyr; Dillamore+2026) is an "Omega_b +-1"-class effect on the 700-Myr window: bar-phase lag vs a constant bar 10 deg (330 Myr), 30 (500), 40-50 (700); constant Omega +1.5 gives 15-30 / 50-80 deg. Orbit offset 0.19 kpc / 6 km/s at 350 Myr, 0.74 kpc / 45 km/s at 700 Myr.
  • To first order degenerate with Omega and angle: Omega_fit = Omega_today + ~1.2, alpha_fit = alpha_today + ~10 deg. So a slowing bar pushes the equivalent present-day angle LOWER (strong-bar 12.5 -> ~2-5 deg today); it sharpens, not relieves, the angle tension.
  • It cannot mimic the strong bar: with fixed amplitude and S ~ 1/Omega the past bar is weaker (A S^3 0.90 at 350 Myr, 0.80 at 700 Myr); the demand is an rms outer torque (R 4-7 kpc), not a phase. Expected effect after re-optimisation: hundreds, not 2500.
  • The 10-10 slowing test (old frame, fixed params, Omega 31-34 not bracketing) is not a verdict.
  • No resonance crossing in the window (Omega 36 -> 33 over 700 Myr; 1:1 at ~24.4). Inference to check: the published-bar peaks at 32-33 and 44-46 are an m = 2 alias pinned by the bar phase at the ~235-256-Myr pericentre.

docs.title: Lessons from metal_poor_disk
docs.text: Rewinds are phase-sensitive; model (bar-history) uncertainty dominates data errors (island width 10x errors); mock closure must include the mismatched history; coherence over (Omega, eta) is patchy -> scan Omega at <= 0.5 with CRN, never NM from one start; forward modelling beats rewinding. The stream's memory of the bar ~ 2 circulation periods of the near-1:1 angle (360-380 Myr): it measures the window-mean Omega and pericentre phases at 230-350 Myr; eta only weakly (through the oldest, worst-fitted debris). Treat eta as a nuisance with prior 0.003 +- 0.001-0.0015; re-parametrise by the window-mean Omega_w = Omega_today + eta Omega^2 .

docs.title: Strategy (decision tree)
docs.text:
A. Fixed-parameter slowing-bar sprays (CRN, 32k): 4 bases (strong 12.5, 25; published 27/44.8, 22/33) x eta {0.001,0.002,0.003,0.005} x Omega_today offsets {-2.4..+0.6} + constant-Omega controls: ~100 sprays, ~20-35 min on 8 cores. Within +-150 -> nuisance; published gain > 300 -> go to C first; loss > 500 everywhere -> only B matters. B. Mock closure (decisive for "strong bar = artefact of constant Omega"): truth = published bar 27 deg, eta 0.003, Omega_today 33 (and 39); fit with the constant-Omega design (A, S free) + control on a constant published-bar truth in the present set-up; 3 runs ~15 h. A S^3 >= 2.5 and gap >~ 1000 -> artefact; A S^3 <= 1.6 and gap <= 300 -> strong bar stands. Fable predicts 1.4-1.7. C. Joint refit, A = S = 1, (Omega_w, eta) free with eta prior, angle 27 and 12.5: 2 x ~5 h. Gap < 500 -> strong-bar claim withdrawn;

1500 -> strong bar required regardless of history. D. If C is ambiguous: re-score at age cuts 500 / 700 (no new sprays). Pitfalls: amplitude/length convention; 1-Myr time table (1.9 deg of bar per step; check once with a finer table); Omega_today vs Omega_fit when comparing with the literature; PM prior matters (LMC degeneracy); differences below ~300 need 4 x 256k at matched seeds. Against: A-C may only confirm a few-hundred nuisance; misfits common to every model will not be touched by eta.

docs.title: Fable: how to demonstrate (1) no-bar fails, (2) the bar must rotate, (3) the bar is non-standard (2026-10-22)
docs.text: Read-only review. Numbers spot-checked by Claude against results/streams/fixedbar_20261021/result.json (from25 -23859 at Omega_b 33.4; from25_om27 -27138 at 30; from25_om42 -23225 at 44.8) and results/plot_data/paper_models.json (old-frame axisymmetric variants -25450 to -26455).

docs.title: Exists vs missing
docs.text:
• Current setup: inflated 9-D profile 12.5 deg -20598 (se 17), 25 deg -21669; published bar at 27 deg, Omega_b free: -23225 (44.8), -23859 (33.4).
  • No-bar: only old frame/score (S2, d free to 5.95, 32k): Hunter axi refit -3541 +- 196 vs 16-deg bar; McMillan17 and q/disc/v_c variants 3300-4300 below. Not quotable in the current setup.
  • Static bar: never optimised; fixed-parameter excess test only (static ph90 recovers 0.63 at 25 deg, 0.25 at 12.5).
  • Published bar at low angle: never refit (unrefit -3808 at the 12.5 best).
  • Mock T2c0 (truth = published bar, 27 deg): free 9-D fit returns A 0.90, S 1.16 (A S^3 = 1.4) and lands 303 below the truth check.

docs.title: A. Logic
docs.text:
Common rule: same catalogue, box, score, priors, frame and optimiser (profile_nm.NM, CRN, 40/chain, 64k search, 4 x 256k finals),

= 4 chains incl. starts at the barred best's nuisances. Quote Delta lnL + prior (256k, 4 seeds), star-bootstrap sd, T ~ 2, segment split, and nuisance values side by side. 1. Axisymmetric: best no-bar Hunter host (d, PMs, v_c, q, disc_scale free) and McMillan17 (d, PMs free) vs inflated 12.5. Visual: data vs model tracks; cumulative Delta lnL vs phi1; flat L_z(t). Referee: optimised as hard; other potentials; LMC (force ratio ~0.01 vs 0.10 demanded). 2. Rotating: static bar (Omega_b = 0; orientation, A, S, nuisances free) vs rotating best; plus published-bar Omega_b sensitivity and the excess-pattern test. Risk: if an optimised static pattern recovers ~90%, the claim becomes "a specific phase history". 3. Non-standard: published bar (A = S = 1), Omega_b and nuisances free: gap 2627 at 27 deg (exists), 12.5/17.5 deg (new); force-ratio profile; mu_alpha* residual at phi1 7-19; mock T2c0 shows the fit does not inflate a standard bar.

docs.title: B. Figures
docs.text:
• F1 data vs three best models (no-bar [new], published 27 deg Omega_b 44.8, inflated 12.5): Delta phi2, mu_alpha*, mu_delta, v_los.
  • F2 residuals + cumulative Delta lnL vs phi1.
  • F3 likelihood ladder (all variants, error = star-bootstrap sd, segment-stacked; reference bars: optimisation floor ~300, T2c0 gap).
  • F4 what the bar does: (a) force ratio vs R; (b) L_z(t): no-bar, published, fitted; (c) lnL vs Omega_b (0 [new], 33-35, 44.8).
  • F5 (optional) mock calibration.

docs.title: C. New runs (8 workers)
docs.text:
• P1 no-bar fit: fixedbar_fit-style with amp 0 (barred branch so axi_variant is honoured), 7-D incl. disc_scale; 4 chains ~5.4 h; McMillan17 3-D in 2 extra chains.
  • P2 published bar at 12.5 and 17.5 deg, 2 chains each, ~5.4 h (P1 + P2 together ~8-9 h).
  • P3 static bar 8-D, 4 chains, ~5.4 h (optional Omega_b 10, 20: +5 h).
  • P4 mock calibration on T2c0 with the fixedbar fit, ~3 h (+ ~5 h no-bar-truth mock, lower priority).
  • Cheap: per-star re-scores for bootstrap sd and segments; LMC on/off pair at 12.5 best.

docs.title: D. Wording (pending numbers in brackets)
docs.text:
1. Best axisymmetric MW (d, PMs, v_c, q, disc mass free) fits worse than the best barred model by [P1], against sd ~80 and floor ~300; deficit in the PM turn at phi1 > 17.
  2. Static bar (orientation, strength free) worse by [P3]; static copy of the required force recovers <= 63%, co-rotating 100%; published-bar fit changes by 3900 between Omega_b 30 and 45.
  3. Published bar, Omega_b 20-50 and nuisances free: worse by 2627 at 27 deg [and P2 at 12.5-17.5], needs Omega_b 44.8; required force 2.5-3.5x published at 4-7 kpc; on a published-bar mock the same fit returns A S^3 = 1.4.

docs.title: Against the plan
docs.text: ~16 h on null fits whose sign is predictable. Fable still recommends P1 and P2 (matched no-bar fit was demanded by the 10-16 Codex review; old-frame number not quotable); P3 droppable with claim 2 softened to "co-rotating (fixed-parameter test)".

docs.title: Fable review: global fitting design for stream 54 (2026-10-20)
docs.text: Read-only review of the pipeline (profile_nm, search_wave, emulator, score) and the journal 2026-10-17..20. Claude verified: stream_batch.py calls make_spray without a frame (baumgardt default) and records frame="baumgardt"; emulator_design.load rejects runs with nrel != 256000; ~2729 stored run records. Journal seed scatter at 256k is sd 45-240 (2026-10-16/17), wider than the 45-65 quoted below.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
• profile_nm gives a profile of local optima (start-dependent: 27.5 deg -29970 local vs -23028 from the 12.5 family; T2c0 best 303 short of the truth); no posterior, no marginalisation, finals are lower bounds of the profile.
  • Families (A~1.8/S~0.9 vs A~1.2/S~1.4/q~0.8), Omega-vc and angle-d degeneracies; edge pile-ups (d, vc, q) are misspecification absorbed by nuisances, not a sampler problem.
  • Noise: sd ~300 at 32k, 60-90 at 128k, 45-65 (journal: 45-240) at 256k; correlated across stars; CRN reliable >= 0.05 unit.
  • Emulator: constant-mean Matern GP; random K-fold CV cannot detect unsampled ridges; T2 missed by 16 deg; maxima optimistic by 430-1900. load() is 256k-only; stream_batch is baumgardt-only.
  • Overconfidence: block/star bootstrap ratio 400-700/65-92; block bootstrap confounds signal heterogeneity along the stream with dependence, so 30-70 is not yet a calibrated T.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Target: generalised (Gibbs) posterior pi_T ~ prior x exp(lnL_jk/T); T = 1 is not computable (sim noise, GP error); T calibrated (sandwich T = J/H from block bootstrap of seed-averaged per-star vectors minus sim noise; Fable's rough estimate T ~ 100-200), checked on mocks; report at T_cal/3, T_cal, 3T_cal.
  • GP surrogate used only as a proposal; posterior verified on sprays by importance weights exp[(lnL_sim - mu_GP)/T] at 256k, iterated as population Monte Carlo until ESS/N >= 0.3 (needs sigma_GP <~ T in the posterior region).
  • Multi-fidelity as heteroskedastic noise (32k/128k/256k observe the same jackknife-corrected function; learned 32k offset); history-matching waves at 32k (implausibility cut I < 3 + cT; 70% NROY, 20% global Sobol never excluded, 10% held out); independent seeds for surrogate data, CRN only for NM polishing.
  • Multimodality: global 32k Sobol wave; NM polishing per stratum + transferred family; parallel tempering on the surrogate.
  • Sampler in logit(unit) coordinates (edges). Validation: frozen rules, 4 well-specified + 2 misspecified mocks, coverage.

docs.title: Budget (14 cores)
docs.text: Stage 0 (no sprays): T calibration on T2c0 mock catalogues, 32k->256k jackknife offset; ~3 h re-scoring. Stage 1 (method on T2c0): ~1230 stored evaluations + 2 x 100 x 256k = 50 core-h (~4 h wall). Stage 2 (real, step2): 32k wave 256 + 3 NROY waves + PMC 4 x 150 x 256k ~ 200 core-h (~15 h wall). Stage 3 (coverage): 450-650 core-h (~1.5-2 days). Reuse: ~765 step2/gravity21 runs enter the real-data GP directly.

docs.title: Decision points / risks
docs.text: Stage 0: if the sandwich T on T2c0 is not ~1, block bootstrap cannot calibrate T. Stage 1: if ESS/N < 0.1 after 3 rounds, switch to per-stratum GPs or a 128k noisy-MH run (~3.5 days). Stage 2: edge pile-up expected -> report conditional on the band; then inner-potential variants as extra dimensions. Risks: surrogate accuracy vs T; T is a calibration choice; undiscovered ridges.

docs.title: Against its own recommendation
docs.text: The posterior will probably say what the profile says (angle broad at T ~ 100; Omega 31.5-34, A >~ 1.1). A profile with sandwich-corrected intervals plus 2-3 more angles and multi-start polishing costs ~10% and is defensible; the posterior is worth it only for joint (Omega, A, S, q) constraints or to remove local-optimum fragility by design.

docs.title: Fable: STREAMFINDER selection imprints, Gaia DR3 re-selection, selection-aware modelling (2026-10-23)
docs.text: Read-only plan. Paper facts from arXiv 1804.11339 (Malhan & Ibata 2018), 2012.05245 (Ibata+2021), 2311.17202 (Ibata+2024). Claude re-checked the members' per-bin statistics (3681 members): counts per 2 deg from phi1 -2: 656, 685, 341, 120, 43, 19, 28, 49, 142, 243, 344, 329, 257, 188, 57; sd(dphi2) 2.85, 2.82, 2.61, 2.04, 0.82, 0.60, 0.60, 0.72, 1.09, 1.38, 1.43, 1.87, 2.16, 2.84, 3.59; template width 50 pc at 5.4 kpc = 0.53 deg.

docs.title: STREAMFINDER selection (verified from the papers)
docs.text: Per-star likelihood: 20-deg DB98 orbit template (Gaussian width 50 pc) x 12.5-Gyr PARSEC SSP at one of 7 [Fe/H] (-2.2..-0.7, sets the distance) x parallax x PM x v_los vs an empirical per-tile GMM field; threshold ln L-hat > 19.8 (6 sigma); G0 < 20, A_V < 2; GCs masked at 2 r_t; Ibata+2021: "for |b| < 20 the sample is highly incomplete and the selection is not remotely objective". Members are orbit-, isochrone-, distance- and contrast-dependent; the threshold is non-linear in local density.

docs.title: Imprints on stream 54 and tests
docs.text:
1. Threshold non-linearity: in the phi1 6-14 gap sd(dphi2) collapses to 0.6-0.8 deg (~template width) vs 2-2.9 near the cluster and 1.1-2.2 at the knee -> only template-ridge stars survive; G and extinction do not explain it. Gap likely a real dip amplified by the threshold.
  2. Orbit-template bias of the sky ridge at phi1 6-13 (where the dphi2 misfit lives).
  3. Distance/parallax/CMD coupling: STREAMFINDER per-star distances 5.3 -> 3.2 kpc along the stream; member parallaxes and CMDs are shaped by them (explains the +0.063 mas near-cluster excess; knee distance from members unreliable).
  4. Single-[Fe/H] isochrone vs omega Cen's spread; RGB nearly absent (29 stars at G < 15).
  5. No members at b < 13.2; 1.6-deg cluster mask.
  6. Gaia completeness/quality fractions vary with scanning; measure from the field (gaiaunlimited M10 map installed). Not an artefact: the knee PM (M5 check, 2026-10-10).

docs.title: Re-selection design
docs.text: WSDB gaia_dr3 footprint phi1 -10..35, |dphi2| < 15, b > 8, G < 20, 5-param+, parallax - 3 sigma < 0.4, broad PM box; ~15-30M rows. (a) CMD window = KDE of omega Cen's own Gaia CMD shifted by a fitted distance ratio f(phi1); (b) spline tracks in PM, ridge, width, parallax, iterated from wide windows; (c) per-bin mixture (stream Gaussian x PM x parallax; field = sideband KDE with a dphi2 gradient) -> p_member, N(phi1), explicit S(phi1, phi2, G, colour, PM); (d) cross-match with the 3681 members. Extra: Gaia RVS, XP [M/H] (G < 16), GALAH DR4, APOGEE DR17; DESI does not reach the field.

docs.title: Modelling with S
docs.text: Weight spray particles by an isochrone/MF-sampled S; extended (Poisson) mixture likelihood in (phi1, dphi2, PMs[, v_los]) with a stars-per-particle nuisance. Gains: far-end density, branch, gap, knee counts. Risks: escaper MF, release history, field model at ~1 star/deg2 in the gap. Keep the conditional score as a cross-check.

docs.title: Staged plan
docs.text: S0 (2-4 h, 1 core, existing 4.8M-row cache results/streams/branch_search_gaia.npz, phi1 5-23): fixed broad windows, per 1-deg bin Gaussian + quadratic in dphi2 -> excess, ridge, width. Excess >= 3x members at 6-13 -> gap is selection; ridge vs members' median tests the dphi2 misfit. S1 (1 h) footprint query; S2 (1-2 d) selection + S + cross-match (recovery > 90% at 14-26, > 70% elsewhere, purity > 70%); S3 (1 d) density profile, ridge, width, ZP-corrected statistical parallax, stream-excess CMD; S4 (2-4 d) forward-model S on stored sprays (3 LF/MF variants, 2 release histories) before any refit. Pitfalls: crowding/scanning at b 8-15; cluster mask and extra-tidal halo; parallax ZP (L21 per star); DR3 PM systematics ~0.02 mas/yr; CMD width from the cluster, not an isochrone; SFD only (Bayestar stops at dec -30); no circularity (do not initialise tracks or CMD from members only). Against: the bar signal sits in the knee kinematics (already shown not to be an artefact); the density adds information but is degenerate with mass-loss history, escaper MF and the field model. Build the density likelihood only if S3 measures the profile at >= 3 sigma per 2-deg bin and S4 shows LF/release sensitivity below the model differences.

docs.title: Fable: review of the stream-fitting note (paper/stream_fits_note, local only; 2026-10-22)
docs.text: Read-only review; numbers re-derived from result.json/profile.json/manifest/state.json. Claude verified the key points (strong-bar profile: 2 chains per angle, 128k search; fixedbar chain spread 3913; Hunter2024 doi/arXiv real via ADS) and applied: - Table: strong-bar chains 4 -> 2; strong-bar search at 1.28e5, Omega_b 30-40, A 0.6-2, S 0.8-1.5 stated. - "Chains end <~300 apart" was wrong: chains started elsewhere end 600-1000 lower (no-bar 934, published 12.5 1007, 27 deg 3913); 300 is the mock optimisation shortfall. Text, ladder caption and discussion corrected. - Seed sd 15-60 (not 10-30); bootstrap sd 35-80 measured only for strong-bar angle differences (assumed elsewhere). - Static bar "worse than no bar" -> "no better than no bar" (480 < no-bar chain spread; disc fixed vs free); rotation evidence is the 5683 gap plus the excess-pattern test. - No-bar best also at q, distance and mu_alpha box edges; McMillan at distance and PM edges: stated. - Asymmetric optimisation effort (strong bar inherited earlier searches): stated; gaps may be too large by hundreds. - T ~ 2 measured for differences 400-1200: extrapolation stated. - Mock: A S^3 = 1.4, 300 short, earlier set-up; current-set-up mock check still to do. - Hercules 0.01-0.02 (not ~0.01); static bar stronger (not as strong); sky offset 2-3 deg at phi1 5-15; published-bar mu_alpha 1-3 mas/yr; inner force ratio 1.1-1.3; no-bar columns 4 and 6; 17.5 vs 12.5 (150) treated as equal. - Citations added: Reid & Brunthaler 2020, Bennett & Bovy 2019. - Figures: gallery residual legend moved, residual ylim -5..4, contours thicker; ladder legend moved off the published curve. Open (UNVERIFIED): primary source for the Hercules m=2 strength 0.01-0.02; star bootstrap for the null-model differences.

docs.title: Fable review: path to a global posterior, revisited after Stage 0 (2026-10-22)
docs.text: Claude verified: 256k final seed sd per angle 35/25/24/14/30/30 (profile_step2); a 9-D quadratic fitted to the 165 step-2 128k evaluations within Delta lnL < 1000 (55 coefficients) leaves residual sd 48 (~ the 128k noise) -> locally quadratic.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: At the calibrated T ~ 2 the posterior's 68% region spans Delta lnL ~ T chi2_9(0.68)/2 ~ 10, below the 256k simulation noise (sd 14-35): no spray-verified T~2 posterior can exist, and its widths (angle ~0.3-1 deg, Omega_b ~0.1, A ~0.02, q ~0.01; d and v_c truncated at band edges) are 50-500x smaller than the shifts between model variants (bar model: angle 12.5 -> 27, Omega_b 33.5 -> 44.8, gap 2627; frame change 6000 at fixed params). Full surrogate + PMC at T ~ 2 is infeasible (ESS/N = exp(-(30/2)^2) ~ 0; a surrogate accurate to ~2 in lnL would need ~22,000 sprays).

docs.title: Ranking
docs.text:
1. Laplace covariance from a designed local quadratic regression (~200 points around the best + replicates; 128k: ~1.6 h, 256k: ~3.4 h on 14 cores), labelled "statistical, within-model" -- for the FINAL model only.
  2. Profiles (exist for angle; an Omega_b profile at 12.5 deg ~2.7 h is optional).
  3. Generalised posterior with a chosen T_sys ~ 300-1000: computable with the 10-20 design (~200 core-h) but T_sys is a free choice and misspecification shifts rather than broadens the optimum: presentation device only.
  4. Full surrogate + PMC at T ~ 2: infeasible.

docs.title: Which model, when
docs.text: Neither the inflated-bar 9-D model nor the published-bar model is final. Build the model first (bar-locked / dark-bar component, Hercules check), then compute the covariance once for the surviving model. The honest "corner" now is a scatter of best-fit points across model variants (systematic error), with ellipses too small to draw.

docs.title: Against
docs.text: A referee may want a marginal posterior; a tempered T_sys ~ 300-500 posterior would show 17.5 deg as a ~1-sigma neighbour; rejected because T_sys is arbitrary and the dominant error is a shift between discrete model variants.

docs.title: Fable review: selection-aware score and a Gaia search for the 25-deg second branch (2026-10-21)
docs.text: Claude verified: on-tube (|dphi2-med|<3 deg, |dPM|<2) / second-branch (pmra < member median - 3) debris fractions per 4-deg phi1 bin 6-22: 12.5 deg 0.56-0.70 / 0.12-0.18; 25 deg 0.39-0.47 / 0.28-0.38; bin/streams/m5_independent_selection.py (ABCD background method) exists.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• The 12.5-vs-25 gap (1071) is mostly debris off the members' tube, not track shape. First-order tube normalisation gives the 25-deg model back +805 (S = +-2 MAD), +684 (3), +595 (4), +398 (6 MAD); 60-70% from phi1 18-28.
  • The branch occupies the same region in both models (amplitude differs): d 4.0-4.6 kpc (track 5.0-5.4), dphi2 -4..-9 deg south of the track (only 10-19% overlaps the members' sky), pmra 5-6 mas/yr more negative, pmdec within ~1, v_los 30-60 km/s lower at phi1 18-27; 24% below the data box (dphi2 < -9.5).
  • Member catalogue (Ibata+2024 MRT) has no membership probability or rejected candidates.

docs.title: Test 2 (ranked first): Gaia DR3 search
docs.text:
Region A per 4-deg phi1 bin from the model's branch PMs (e.g. phi1 6-10: pmra -14.3..-9.1, pmdec -10.2..-8.0; ... 18-22: -17.1..-14.2, -11.6..-10.2), dphi2 -13..-1 excluding +-2.5 deg of the track, parallax soft cut (0.18-0.27 incl. ZP), members' CMD locus shifted ~0.4 mag brighter (fit the shift), G 16-19.8, ruwe < 1.4, dereddened. One WSDB pull, selections in Python. Background ABCD: PM sidebands -5 mas/yr, sky sidebands dphi2 -25..-13 and +4..+9 (avoid stream 45 at +10..+14), subtract model leakage (report with/without). Statistic R = branch excess / track excess: predicted ~1.0 (25 deg) vs ~0.35 (12.5),

= 6 sigma apart; pre-register 5-sigma excess, R, CMD shift + mean parallax (4.0-4.6 kpc), pmra gradient along phi1 (strongest discriminant vs field), Gaia RVS v_los at phi1 > 18. Clean bins phi1 6-14. Outcomes: R ~ 1 -> branch real, current score unfair, angle open, score track+branch with a full Gaia selection; R ~ 0.3 -> 12.5 stands with its own weak branch confirmed; no excess -> both models over-produce 250-500 Myr off-track debris -> release history suspect.

docs.title: Test 1: selection-aware score (sensitivity bound, not a likelihood)
docs.text: L_i = [(1-eps) f(w_i|u_i) + eps/|S(u_i)|] / [(1-eps) F_S(u_i) + eps], F_S = integral_S f(w|u); S empirical and fixed before scoring: per 2-deg phi1 bin, +-k MAD around members' medians in (dphi2, pmra, pmdec), k = 2,3,4,6 as a family; F_S as hard particle count first; floor F_S at 10 effective particles; no model-dependent S. Mock check on the 20 T2 catalogues truncated by the same recipe (maximum must stay at 27). Can soften the 12.5 preference, never establish 25.

docs.title: Against its own ranking
docs.text: Test 2 rests on the models' absolute 250-500 Myr debris (release history never varied); a null means "release model wrong", and the leakage correction re-introduces the model. Test 1 is cheaper (hours) and bounds the sensitivity now.

docs.title: Fable review: step-2 design (2026-10-20)
docs.text: Read-only review of commit 508b80e (gravity21 frame, v_c prior, step2 design, profile_nm changes). Claude verified items 1, 2, 4 against the code before acting; items 2 and 4 fixed in the following commit (profile_nm --transfer; strict manifest check).

docs.title: Verified issues
docs.text:
1. Box: the real-data profile (profile_real_20261019) and run_real_chain.sh use --box data; the 32k frame tests used the wide box (~3.7 ln L per background star more volume). Wide-box numbers are not comparable with -20498; use --box data.
  2. No family transfer across angles: starts() only takes runs within +-2.5 deg, so the 12.5-deg family is never tried at 17.5-27.5; chains at 25 and 27.5 share starts. Fix: second chain = global best moved to the angle.
  3. All step2 starts sit at the band edge (d unit 1.0) and vc/q edges; with STEP0 0.1 and budget 30 a chain that must climb ~7000 measures how far it got, not the profile.
  4. Resume check compared only keys of the new manifest (optional keys vc_prior could be dropped silently). Cached evaluations are keyed by run id: do not change start directories between resumes.
  5. W_sun = 7.25 (Schoenrich) while Sgr A* mu_b = -0.219 gives 4.74047 x 0.219 x 8.275 = 8.59 km/s; one 32k spray settles it.
  6. Frame plumbing otherwise consistent (placement, projection, r0 in axi_variant and r_cr, segment_profile vc_prior).

docs.title: Design points
docs.text:
1. The v_c prior N(233, 7) is cosmetic under the untempered score (1.7 at 220 vs score gradients 1e2-1e3 per km/s); effectively a hard band 220-250. Same for the d prior inside the band.
  2. R0 has angle-sized leverage: ~1000-1800 ln L per 1 sigma (33 pc) at fixed parameters, comparable with the angle contrast (640-910). Free R0 with prior N(8.275, 0.034) and V_tot tied, or at least a +-33 pc sensitivity; Oyama+2024 mu_l is a smaller version (~-600).
  3. d, vc, q edges all point one way (less bound omega Cen orbit); banding d pushes the compensation into vc, q, A, S. Inner-potential terms (disc_scale, bar mass/eta) are the physical absorbers; test them before the full profile.

docs.title: Recommended order
docs.text: A. Recovery test (~2-3 h, 8 cores): 32k NM, 4 angles (12.5, 17.5, 27.5, 32.5) x 2 chains (one from the other family), budget 60-80, data box, gravity21, step2 band. Recovery to within ~500-1000 of the d=5.70 best -> band harmless, run the profile; deficit > ~2000 with edges -> misspecification, go to C. B. 128k profile only after A(i): data box, budget >= 40, starts from A, 4 x 256k finals, segment_profile readout. C. Inner-potential variants in the same campaign: disc_scale as a 10th coordinate (optionally bar_eta) in A-style runs at 12.5 and 27.5; does any remove the Delta phi2 offsets and the d/vc/q edge pull? LMC after C. D. One-spray checks (32k): W_sun 8.59; R0 +-33 pc; Oyama V_tot. They set the systematic floor for any angle contrast. E. Fix items 1, 4 (and 2) before launching.

docs.title: Readiness of the sky+PM <-> CMD (dm) iteration: Fable and Codex (2026-10-23)
Fable (scratch tests on the cached footprint)
docs.text:
• Template vs colour-centring difference is marginal with x2 inflated errors: per-bin (centring - template)/sigma = +1.9, -0.2, -0.6, -1.0, +0.8, -0.1 at phi1 4..24 (chi2 5.7/6), and not one-signed.
  • LF tilt: not the cause (alpha unconstrained, dm moves <= 0.12). Common colour/reddening shift: not the cause (moves both estimators the same way; full-CMD fit pins the stream-template colour offset at 0.00 +- 0.02). Annulus E(B-V)_SFD median 0.132, stream 0.065-0.08.
  • Background variants swing centring by 0.2-0.25 and the template by 0.1 at phi1 2-18; default 5-14 quadratic least biased.
  • Driver of the split: faint stream excess (observed G0 > 18.8) redder than the shifted template by +0.04..+0.07 in every bin; centring dominated by G0 19.0-19.6 (14-18: +0.31 / 0.00 / -0.12 / -0.25 for faint limits 18.6 / 19.0 / 19.3 / 19.6); template never sees those stars at 10-18 and is itself unstable to its faint edge (0.2 swing). Cause (faint BP/RP bias annulus vs field, or background at the faint red end) not disentangled.
  • Recommended driver: template fit on the calibrated domain, errors x2, anchored dm(0) = 0, 1-2 parameters, held constant beyond the last accepted bin: linear dm = -0.0266 phi1 (chi2 4.8/5) or quadratic 0.0062 phi1 - 0.0016 phi1^2 (2.9/4). Centring line gives dm(0) = +0.41 (unphysical); anchored centring chi2 18.4/5.
  • Mask tolerance: a 0.3 mag dm error = 0.4-0.8 of the k = 2 MS half-width, 1.3 sigma on the TO/SGB -> one pass ~ fixed point.
  • Freeze: template, PM-control scaling, per-bin faint domain edge and dm grid centre (at iteration 0), bands, bins, thresholds, nulls, k, g_bright, errors, reddening, anchor/form; fix the phi1 13 sky bin before the loop.
  • Tests: stop rule + CMD-pass change < 2% + accepted set unchanged; two starting relations -> same end; nulls through the loop; end-to-end injection (bias < 0.1, coverage >= 60% with x2 errors); MS vs TO split within 1.5 sigma; faint-colour check (G-RP ridge, null-field slices).
  • Against: if the faint red offset is a template artefact, faint-MS values (-0.25 at 12-16) are right and the anchored template line is too shallow by 0.1-0.2 at 8-16; mask insensitive at that level, published dm should wait for the faint-colour check.

docs.title: Codex (read code + JSON)
docs.text:
• Not ready. Estimators use different magnitude ranges (template faint limit ~18.4 at phi1 20; centring to 19.6) -> compare on common support. Centring: first zero crossing, no detection requirement, fixed background in errors. Injection reuses the fitted background (does not test background errors). Background has no footprint-area correction for partial bands. Sky upper-branch exclusion uses the bin-centre position for a 4-deg bin; sky retains a +-2 deg anchor to the marked track.
  • Provisional: centring straight line uncapped (+0.41 - 0.046 phi1) as a selection coordinate only; no quadratic/spline.
  • Protocol: freeze the measurement definition (domain and MS/TO split must not move with the incoming line); full-loop injections/nulls; stability of selection (two successive iterations within tolerance, widths/borders/accepted set stable, multiple starts, detect two-cycles); reproducible outputs with hashes; driver must reject < 3 accepted bins (currently silently returns old coefficients).
  • Against: centring may be the biased one (at phi1 4 template MS and TO agree at -0.04/-0.12, centring +0.21).

docs.title: Mask track smoothing (spline clip) and orbit-start masks: Fable and Codex (2026-10-23)
docs.text: Question: is clipping the per-iteration offset spline (smooth_offset) to the accepted offsets' range a correct fix, and should the orbit-start (McMillan17 orbit, no anchor) masks be adopted as standard?

docs.title: Fable (scratch reruns of stream_masks.py)
docs.text:
• Clip = band-aid. Root defect: LSQ cubic spline (6-deg knots) evaluated across gaps between accepted bins. Default run: pmra bins at phi1 7-17 never accepted (1-3.9 sigma); spline bridges 5 -> 19 and oscillates (applied offset at phi1 11 per iteration -0.41, +1.14, -1.68, +0.01, -0.75, -0.49), hitting the +-1.5 anchor at 9-14. The current default pmra track at 7-17 is spline overshoot stopped by the anchor. Same in the sky: a lone accepted dphi2 bin at phi1 3-5 gives spline offsets up to -99/+11 deg (anchor-limited). Ill-conditioned even between adjacent accepted bins (+58.9 mas/yr at phi1 3).
  • Clip fills gaps with the extreme accepted offset (non-local). Orbit-start clipped run: pmra at 9/13/15 = -5.83/-7.06/-7.82 vs orbit -7.25/-8.98/-9.88 (it did not stay on the orbit; it was pushed by the clip).
  • Pooled unbinned pmra fit over phi1 7-17, ridge residual from the final track: current default +1.29 +- 0.19 (default centre 1.3 mas/yr below the ridge); default+clip -0.12; default+linear -0.19; default+hold 0.00 (the marked start was on the ridge); orbit+clip +0.16 (slope +0.31/deg); orbit+linear/hold +0.44/+1.15.
  • Recommended: (1) multi-scale acceptance: failed bins refitted on +-3 then +-5 deg windows (slope term); (2) bridge gaps > 4 deg linearly, drop the clip; (3) pooled windows only inside the single-bin-accepted range (otherwise phi1 29 drifts); (4) sky fits at phi1 >= 13 only; (5) guard: |spline offset| <= 2 x max accepted |mu|. Default + pooled + linear reproduces the current default outside 7-17 to <= 0.2 (0.33 at 27) and puts 7-17 on the ridge (+0.03 +- 0.21).
  • Do not adopt orbit-start clipped masks (pmra 7-17 set by the clip; FREE settings change the fits, e.g. pmdec widths 0.66-0.74 vs 0.33-0.46 at 5-13). It does establish: pmdec and pmra at -1..5 and 19-27 agree with the default (data-driven).
  • Tests: regression vs current default; ridge residual < 0.3 at 7-17; start test with identical settings (< 0.5); null with a +3 mas/yr displaced track; end-bin stability; guard never fires.
  • Against: the 7-17 ridge is only 4-7 sigma in 6-10 deg windows; starts still differ by 1.0 at phi1 9; a wide mask with no claimed centre may be the honest product there.

docs.title: Codex (read code + JSON)
docs.text:
• Clip = numerical guard, not a fix; plateaus across unsupported intervals; default movement can be iteration feedback.
  • Do not adopt yet: not converged (pmra phi1 27 moved 0.28 in the last iteration); stopping rule uses per-bin offsets, not track changes; fit_pm truncation/normalisation, post-hoc floor, conditional errors; borders computed against pre-update offsets.
  • Some "strong" near-cluster pmra bins fail cuts (phi1 -1 width 1.73 > cap; phi1 3 at 3.9 sigma, floor width).
  • Recommended: gap-aware linear interpolation (bridge <= 6 deg, taper at segment ends), same for widths; then a normalised, penalised, pooled unbinned spline likelihood across phi1 including weak bins. Convergence: two iterations < 0.05 mas/yr, 0.1 deg, 5% width. Version outputs with code/input hashes.

docs.title: Mask borders for the Gaia cross-selection: Fable and Codex (2026-10-23)
docs.text: Question: a robust, reproducible, minimally circular way to set the borders (centre, half-width vs phi1) of the dphi2, pmra*, pmdec masks (bin/streams/gaia_xsel_marked.py), and whether the user's two candidate pmdec borders (RED narrow; GREEN broad, fanning envelope) are supported. Claude re-ran Fable's check script (numbers reproduced).

docs.title: Fable (with quick measurements on the cache)
docs.text:
• pmdec (sky-lower + pmra masks; 1 Gaussian deconvolved with per-star errors + empirical off-sky background): intrinsic width <= 0.1 mas/yr at phi1 14-18, 0.41 +- 0.06 at 18-22, 0.50 +- 0.10 at 20-24, 0.8 +- 0.3 at 24-28, unconstrained at 26-30; same for G < 18.5 and 18.5-20 (error model fine). Growth exceeds the distance gradient -> kinematic fanning.
  • The by-eye tracks are biased: pmdec centre +0.3..+0.6 mas/yr above the marked track at 16-22 (fit -9.26 +- 0.08 at 18-22 vs track -9.63); pmra ~1 mas/yr too negative at 22-26 (+1.25 +- 0.21 at 22-24); sky centre +0.7 -> -0.6 deg across 14-24 (s 0.6-1.0 deg).
  • RED upper border cuts the stream at 18-24 (band between red and green upper borders: +44, 3.5 s; +54, 4.4 s). No second, lower-pmdec component: dBIC(1 vs 2) -24..-13 (1 preferred everywhere); green-minus-red below holds -1, -1, -4 stars at 14-24 and +17, +12 at 24-30 = tail of one broadening component.
  • Fixed +-1 mas/yr is ~5 sigma at 14-18 and ~1 sigma at 24-28. Use centre +- k sigma_tot(phi1, G), sigma_tot^2 = s_int^2 + e_i^2; S/N-optimal k = 1.4 (k 1.2-1.8 within 2.5 per cent); figure k = 1.5-2; counts from mixture amplitudes, not masks.
  • Procedure: alternating 1-D unbinned fits per adaptive phi1 bin (>= 60 excess stars), empirical background from the unselected dimension, local slope, error deconvolution, wide masks (k = 2.5) while iterating, penalised-spline smoothing of centre and log-width (GCV), width floor, no extrapolation, ~5 iterations; init from the 18-22 VPD peak, step outwards. 3-D mixture in the cleanest bins as a cross-check. Null test already shows spurious N up to 44 +- 26 with zero-width spikes -> floor + regularisation mandatory; 24-30 detections only ~2 sigma above the spurious level.
